item.title: Portable DAC Showdown | HC5 Keeps the Mojo 2 Honest
item.description:

The HC5 leverages Astell&Kern's considerable know-how with AKM decoding hardware and what makes something work as a portable device to create a device that has sparkling performance coupled with the sort of dimensions and practicality to ensure that you will actually use it out and about. It might not have the out-and-out performance of the Mojo 2, but it's more than able to keep it honest and is better suited to a life connected to a phone.

item.title: Eversolo Play CD Edition Streaming Amp Review - Better Than The WiiM Amp Ultra?
item.description:
The Eversolo Play CD is an integrated streaming amplifier and the more ornate of the two Play models. Eversolo by this point needs little introduction. Parent company Zidoo had hinted that it knew a bit about the business of making audio equipment with the Neo streamers but it was the arrival of the original DMP-A6 that removed all doubt. By combining great hardware with a fantastic interface, Eversolo has built some seriously impressive streamers.
The Play models are a completely logical next step in where you might take that expertise. They combine the Eversolo streaming platform with on board amplification to create a self-contained ‘just add speakers’ style box of a type that has been doing very good numbers for a few different companies in recent years. The argument over where ‘amps’ end and ‘all in one’ devices begin is largely moot these days as it’s largely a matter of where the manufacturer feels it should sit rather than any defined aspect of functionality. The Play is described as a streaming amp so for the purposes of this review, that is what it shall be.
This does mean that the Play has to justify its existence (and price premium) over the WiiM family of devices which is rather good at this sort of thing, as well as the lurking presence of the specialist but capable Marantz M1 at similar price points. Can the capability of Eversolo’s streaming platform shine when an amp is added to the package? We need to find out.
Read the full review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/eversolo-play-cd-streaming-amp-review.23236/

item.title: JVC NZ500/RS1200 4K Laser Projector - The BEST IN CLASS!
item.description:
AVForums Editor Phil Hinton reviews the JVC DLA-NZ500/RS1200 D-ILA Native 4K Laser Projector in our latest tech review.
The JVC DLA-NZ500 (DLA-RS1200) is a new breed of native 4K projector from the company, with a much smaller physical chassis, making it much more user-friendly for smaller cinema rooms and installations. This does mean that some features are no longer included, such as 3D playback.
The NZ500 replaces the older lamp-based NP5 model with the BLU-Escent Laser Light technology. One thing that hasn't changed is the superb picture quality on offer, including some of the very best black levels and HDR images from any projector at this price point. Add to this a stunning native contrast, along with HDR Adaptive tone mapping algorithms that squeeze every drop of highlight detail and dynamic range, and you have a very compelling projector proposition at a very attractive price. Plus, you get a fully motorised, newly designed lens system for easy installation and variable aspect ratio screens.
Overall, the JVC DLA-NZ500 (RS1200) is a stunning projector that offers up some of the best image quality available at the price point, with superb deep blacks, shadow detail retrieval and excellent colour accuracy. It is a Best in Class product.

item.title: Epson QB1000B vs Sony and JVC | Which Projector Wins?
item.description:
The Epson QB1000B is an excellent mid-range home cinema projector with the features that most cinephiles are looking for, whether using constant height or multi-aspect ratio screens. While it is not a native 4K projector, even the most eagle-eyed viewers would have trouble telling that it uses RGB 3LCD devices and pixel shift technology to create the faux 8.3 million pixels in a 4K image.
The laser light source has a claimed lifespan of 20,000 hours and is bright; it can pump out close to the advertised 3,300 lumens in the brightest (and most inaccurate) modes. But when calibrated in the Cinema picture preset, it remains bright for larger screens, but with accurate D65 white and colour reproduction. Black levels are also decent, but due to the brightness push, they are not quite as deep and fluid as the Sony and JVC models. But this projector is also a couple of grand cheaper.
The Epson EH-QB1000B is a formidable mid-range home theater projector, offering features often found in more expensive models.
Our editor Phil Hinton provides a deep dive into its picture quality and capabilities, highlighting where this Epson projector excels and its single notable trade-off.
Read the review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/epson-eh-qb1000b-3lcd-laser-projector-review.23129/

item.title: Watch out Apple & Sonos: WiiM Sound Streaming Speaker Review
item.description:
The WiiM Sound Streaming Speaker is unflappably brilliant in a way that’s hard not to admire. It’s a logical and deeply capable way of making use of that carefully evolved software front end and room optimisation to excellent effect. It’s not perfect; the absence of AirPlay is annoying, and we think it could look a bit more exciting (although evidence suggests it doesn’t need to), but its ability to deliver WiiM slickness in a self-contained and keenly priced package is an indisputable Best Buy.

item.title: Sennheiser HDB 630 Review - Is the Hype Justified?
item.description:
The Sennheiser HDB 630 delivers a software platform that has functionality (and no less importantly, a means of using that functionality) that is significantly in advance of rivals. It then also goes about offering a ready-baked solution to underperforming Bluetooth that is likely to require rivals to respond in kind.
The catch is that the headphones sandwiched between these two technical advancements can't always match similarly priced rivals when the playing field is level. They can sound great... but some of the competition can sound better still. For many people, the accompanying hardware and software will be enough for them, but the HDB 630 isn't quite the standout it had the potential to be.
Read Ed Selley's full review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/sennheiser-hdb-630-wireless-headphone-review.23051/

item.title: Is this the BEST Value 4K TV of 2025? 1788 Nits for £649 [TCL C7K / QM7K QD Mini LED TV Review]
item.description:
TCL is shaking up the mid-range market with the TCL C7K Mini LED TV. We're diving deep to find out if this set, starting at just £649 for the 55-inch model, delivers a game-changing combination of features and power. (The QM7K is more or less the same TV and is available in the US.)
While there is no such thing as the perfect TV, and this C7K does have a few of the usual LCD drawbacks like viewing angles and some haloing and blooming, its new HVA panel also produces superb contrast. Add to this some very good local dimming and Mini LED tech, delivering an incredible peak brightness of *1788 nits (5% window)* and solid full-screen brightness of 655 nits, making it an ideal choice for a bright living room. It’s also fully agnostic, supporting HDR10, HDR10+, Dolby Vision, and Dolby Vision IQ.
The TCL C7K is also a very good *Gaming TV*. You get two full-bandwidth HDMI 2.1 ports with support for 4K/144Hz (PC) and 4K/120Hz (PS5/Xbox Series X), alongside AMD FreeSync Premium Pro and a blisteringly fast 4.7ms input lag at 120Hz.
The TCL C7K is an impressive set for the bargain hunter. If your budget is mid-range but your demands are high-end, you simply must audition this TV.
Read the full in-depth review for more data and numbers on AVForums: https://www.avforums.com/reviews/tcl-c7k-55c7k-qd-mini-led-tv-review.23025/

item.title: The BEST TV Under £500? TCL C6K Mini LED Review
item.description:
This is the review of the TCL C6K Mini LED TV, the budget QD-Mini LED that promises to be one of the best value-for-money TVs of the year! But does it truly deliver on its promise? And what is the crucial 'catch' that could be a dealbreaker for some viewers?
In this in-depth video, Phil Hinton dives into the entry-level model of TCL’s premium QD-Mini LED range here in the UK. We’ll show you exactly why the C6K is an *excellent value* option, perfectly suited for a second room, kitchen, or a dedicated gaming setup.
The TCL C6K truly excels in a *bright, well-lit room*, offering genuinely very good picture quality and natural colours for everyday HD SDR content. It’s a fantastic all-rounder when you're not in a darkened cinema room.
*Why Gamers MUST Watch:* The C6K makes a very strong case for itself as a pure gaming display. You get two full-bandwidth *HDMI 2.1* ports, providing console gamers with *4K/120Hz support with Dolby Vision HDR*. For PC gamers, it’s even better: experience stunning visuals at *4K/144Hz* (boostable to 288Hz with Game Accelerator). The input lag is ridiculously fast at *4.9ms with a 120Hz signal*. Throw in AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, and you have a superbly specced gaming screen for the price.
*The Catch:* While it’s great for bright rooms, we found the lower local dimming zone count (just 180 on our 55-inch review sample) means you will see more blooming, Dirty Screen Effect (DSE), and clouding if you try to watch serious movies in dim surroundings. It's simply not a home cinema TV, but a brilliant choice for its sweet spot use cases.
Watch the full video to see our detailed measurements, including its *650 nits peak brightness* and *superb colour accuracy after calibration*. We'll also cover the 2.1 Onkyo sound system, its sleek design, and full HDR format support (including Dolby Vision IQ).
If you’re looking for a cost-effective, high-performance TV for gaming or a bright room, this is one to add to your short list.

For PC gamers, it’s even better: experience stunning visuals at *4K/144Hz* (boostable to 288Hz with Game Accelerator). The input lag is ridiculously fast at *4.9ms with a 120Hz signal*. Throw in AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, and you have a superbly specced gaming screen for the price.
*The Catch:* While it’s great for bright rooms, we found the lower local dimming zone count (just 180 on our 55-inch review sample) means you will see more blooming, Dirty Screen Effect (DSE), and clouding if you try to watch serious movies in dim surroundings. It's simply not a home cinema TV, but a brilliant choice for its sweet spot use cases.
Watch the full video to see our detailed measurements, including its *650 nits peak brightness* and *superb colour accuracy after calibration*. We'll also cover the 2.1 Onkyo sound system, its sleek design, and full HDR format support (including Dolby Vision IQ).
If you’re looking for a cost-effective, high-performance TV for gaming or a bright room, this is one to add to your short list.

item.title: DJI MIC 3 Review: Professional Audio Quality From A Tiny Mic!
item.description:
AVForums Editor, Phil Hinton, reviews the latest DJI Mic 3 and finds some surprising results and a potential disappointment for some users. Read the review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/dji-mic-3-review.22902/
00:00 - Start 00:18 - Unboxing 00:34 - What is the DJI Mic3? 01:42 - What's in the box? 03:11 - All the new Features and Demo 09:32 - DJI Mic 3 Verdict
The DJI Mic 3 is a highly-rated wireless microphone system with its compact size, excellent audio quality, and professional features like 32-bit float recording and timecode support. It is suitable for a wide range of creators, from YouTubers to those on large-scale productions. The system comes with a convenient charging case, magnetic clips, and offers impressive battery life.
Key new features include adaptive gain control modes (Automatic and Dynamic), three voice tone presets (Regular, Rich, and Bright), and two noise cancellation settings. It can connect with up to four transmitters per receiver and eight receivers in total, and offers a transmission range of up to 400 meters. The Mic 3 also features internal dual-file recording for backup and improved dynamic range, and seamless integration with DJI Osmo products via OsmoAudio. While generally lauded, a minor drawback is the absence of a LAV mic input, which was present in previous models. Despite this, the DJI Mic 3 is highly recommended for its ease of use and high-quality audio capture.

item.title: Is This the Best Mini LED TV for 2025? [TCL C8K Review]
item.description:
In this AVForums video, Phil Hinton reviews the TCL C8K Mini LED TV, TCL's 2025 flagship in the UK. It features a sleek design, robust connectivity (including two full-bandwidth HDMI 2.1 ports for gaming), and a premium remote.
Key features and performance aspects include:
*Picture Quality*: The 65-inch C8K uses a new CrystGlow WHVA Panel with improved viewing angles and a low-reflection film. It features a sophisticated Mini LED local dimming system with 1680 zones on the 65-inch model, providing impressive control and minimising halo effects.
*Brightness*: The TV is exceptionally bright, measuring 3170 nits on a 10% window and over 4400 nits on a 5% window in Filmmaker HDR mode.
*Colour Accuracy*: Out-of-the-box accuracy in Filmmaker Mode is good, with excellent greyscale tracking. Wide Colour Gamut performance is strong, covering 91% of DCI-P3 colour volume.
*Gaming Performance*: It offers 4K/144Hz for PC and 4K/120Hz for consoles with Dolby Vision HDR, AMD Freesync Premium Pro, ALLM, and very low input lag (4.8ms at 120Hz).
*Uniformity & Motion*: The panel shows remarkably good uniformity with minimal Dirty Screen Effect. Motion performance is solid for film and broadcast content.
*Audio*: It boasts a 6.2.2 Bang & Olufsen sound system supporting Dolby Atmos and IMAX DTS, offering a wide soundstage.
*Smart TV*: It runs Google TV and now includes UK catch-up apps, a significant improvement for British users, though it lacks a Freely tuner.
In a direct comparison with the Hisense U8Q, the TCL C8K is brighter, has a superior local dimming algorithm, and offers better viewing angles, all while being significantly cheaper. While not flawless (some HDR10 clipping, occasional brightness pumping), its overall image quality, especially for its price point, is described as superb.
For its high performance, excellent local dimming, strong image accuracy, and competitive price, the TCL C8K wins our Best Buy Badge.

media:group.media:title: Is This the Best Mini LED TV for 2025? [TCL C8K Review]
media:group.media:description:
In this AVForums video, Phil Hinton reviews the TCL C8K Mini LED TV, TCL's 2025 flagship in the UK. It features a sleek design, robust connectivity (including two full-bandwidth HDMI 2.1 ports for gaming), and a premium remote.
Key features and performance aspects include:
*Picture Quality*: The 65-inch C8K uses a new CrystGlow WHVA Panel with improved viewing angles and a low-reflection film. It features a sophisticated Mini LED local dimming system with 1680 zones on the 65-inch model, providing impressive control and minimising halo effects.
*Brightness*: The TV is exceptionally bright, measuring 3170 nits on a 10% window and over 4400 nits on a 5% window in Filmmaker HDR mode.
*Colour Accuracy*: Out-of-the-box accuracy in Filmmaker Mode is good, with excellent greyscale tracking. Wide Colour Gamut performance is strong, covering 91% of DCI-P3 colour volume.
*Gaming Performance*: It offers 4K/144Hz for PC and 4K/120Hz for consoles with Dolby Vision HDR, AMD Freesync Premium Pro, ALLM, and very low input lag (4.8ms at 120Hz).
*Uniformity & Motion*: The panel shows remarkably good uniformity with minimal Dirty Screen Effect. Motion performance is solid for film and broadcast content.
*Audio*: It boasts a 6.2.2 Bang & Olufsen sound system supporting Dolby Atmos and IMAX DTS, offering a wide soundstage.
*Smart TV*: It runs Google TV and now includes UK catch-up apps, a significant improvement for British users, though it lacks a Freely tuner.
In a direct comparison with the Hisense U8Q, the TCL C8K is brighter, has a superior local dimming algorithm, and offers better viewing angles, all while being significantly cheaper. While not flawless (some HDR10 clipping, occasional brightness pumping), its overall image quality, especially for its price point, is described as superb.
For its high performance, excellent local dimming, strong image accuracy, and competitive price, the TCL C8K wins our Best Buy Badge.

item.title: Is The Hisense U8Q A BARGAIN FLAGSHIP TV? [Review]
item.description:
Read the Review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/hisense-u8q-65u8q-mini-led-tv-review.22872/ AVForums Editor Phil Hinton gives you a full in-depth review of the Hisense U8Q Mini LED TV. Hisense's ongoing advancements in its high-end Mini LED TV range demonstrate consistent year-on-year enhancements across design, materials, features, and image quality. This progression, however, has led to an increase in pricing, positioning these products in a more premium segment, even as their performance and overall offering are still striving to fully reach that premium standard.
The Hisense U8Q is the best mini LED TV we have seen from the company so far and is better than last year's offering, which is what you would expect to find. It's not perfect, with the usual downsides of the Mini LED LCD technology impacting some aspects of the performance, such as DSE (Dirty Screen Effect) and some local dimming issues in dark room viewing. HDR also looks good for the majority of content I viewed, with decent tone mapping and brightness available. Hisense supports all HDR flavours with HDR10+, HDR10, HLG (Hybrid Log-Gamma) and Dolby Vision and Dolby Vision IQ. We did find some clipping issues with HDR10 content over 1000 nits, and the blooming suppression impacts the overall contrast, but with everything else, the U8Q displays some excellent HDR images that look natural.
Gaming capabilities are enhanced by three HDMI 2.1 (48Gbps) ports. These support 4K/165Hz for PC gaming and 4K/120Hz gaming in Dolby Vision (via Xbox Series X), thanks to the Pentonic SOC. The TV also features a dedicated games menu bar and impressive input lag performance.
The Hisense U8Q is a recommended television for the mass market, particularly for those seeking a bright room TV with very good overall performance, but wait until it is available via sale offers as the MSRP is expensive.

item.title: BEST TV 2025? Panasonic Z95B OLED Review
item.description:
AVForums Editor Phil Hinton reviews the Panasonic Z95B OLED TV. Is this the best TV of 2025? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.
00:00 - Start 00:15 - Let's dive in... 01:37 - First impressions of the Panasonic Z95B - Design and engineering 03:40 - Testing and Measurements 07:07 - Picture Performance 08:22 - Sound Quality 10:14 - Side-by-side comparisons vs. Panasonic Z95A, LG G5, Samsung S95F and BRAVIA 8ii 14:10 - Conclusion
The Panasonic Z95B is an excellent all-in-one TV, delivering accurate SDR and HDR image quality. Its cinematic performance is highlighted by stunning dynamic range, precise colour reproduction, and striking HDR specular details, making it an ideal choice for consumers seeking a high-end viewing experience.
While not without flaws, the Z95B's picture quality is very nearly perfect. It exhibits some minor Dolby Vision issues, specifically posterisation and gradational problems at low-level brightness, particularly when transitioning from black. These issues are similar to those seen on the LG G5, which uses the same Primary RGB Tandem Panel, though significantly less severe than the G5's initial state before its fix. Notably, HDR10 and HLG content are unaffected and achieve reference quality. This observation has been reported to Panasonic, with the hope for a future firmware fix.
While many enthusiasts will have their external sound systems to use with the Z95B, for a wider audience looking for an all-in-one solution for excellent high-end image quality and sound, the new look design also incorporates a new audio layout for a full Dolby Atmos immersive experience tuned by Technics. The new speaker layout is the result of the incorporation of the proprietary Thermalflow panel cooling that allows the set to achieve its stunning HDR image quality.
The Panasonic Z95B marks a significant return to excellence for the Japanese TV engineering team. It delivers stunning out-of-the-box accuracy for both SDR and HDR content, complemented by impressive built-in audio. With UK-specific features like Freely and comprehensive terrestrial catch-up services, alongside a sleek new design, the Z95B is a strong contender for TV of the year, and for home cinema use, it's the Best in Class.

item.title: Can This Little Box Make Your Hi-Fi Sound Amazing? Pro-ject Uni Box S3 Review
item.description:
The Pro-ject Uni Box S3 takes the capable and effective WiiM platform and makes use of it for its own ends. This is not an absolute rival to the in-house streaming amplifiers. Instead, it might be better seen as Pro-Ject taking its effective integrated amplifier platform and making it that little bit more flexible. The result is going to appeal to a different subset of users, but the Uni Box S3 does enough right to ensure it will win many people over.
So, which box suits your needs?

item.title: The BEST Hi-Fi Amp under £1000: WiiM Amp Pro Review
item.description:
AVForums Hi-Fi reviewer Ed Selley gives us a video review of the WiiM Amp Pro. Read the full in-depth review https://www.avforums.com/reviews/wiim-amp-pro-streaming-amplifier-review.22489/
When Ed tested the WiiM Amp, it earned a perfect score almost in spite of the reality that some dedicated amp rivals at a bit more money did sound a bit better. The WiiM Amp Pro reviewed here earns its score completely unambiguously. It brings the same superb selection of functionality along but now sounds decisively better while it does it. Yes, dedicated amp rivals have more inputs, frequently bring a phono stage to the party and might look a bit nicer subjectively but it’s very hard to argue with how much the Amp Pro does and how well it does it. Stop me if you’ve heard this one before but, in a spot of sibling rivalry, the Amp Pro usurps the Amp to become the current Best in Class.

item.title: LG G5 OLED TV Review: Excellent HDR Brightness and Colour Performance (vs LG G4)
item.description:
The LG G5 is the latest 2025 flagship TV and offers stunning HDR images thanks to its new Primary RGB Tandem Panel and Alpha 11 Gen 2 image processing.
There is no such thing as a perfect TV and there are some teething issues with the G5. The first is that the panel comes out of black too quickly which then manifests into floating blacks in some HDR10 and Dolby Vision content. There is also an issue with near-black posterisation and gradational issues, again within some torture test content. This doesn’t happen with all content, but I first noticed this behaviour on a Primary RGB Panel used in a competing brand's demo recently and then again on a G5 that I was able to get hands-on with before this review sample arrived with me.
Thankfully, these issues should get fixed by the engineers at LG and updated via firmware, but don’t base any buying decision on possible fixes, until they are confirmed to have been fixed. Because of these issues, the G5 scores a 9/10. It would have been another 10/10 if these issues hadn’t affected overall image quality. If LG does fix these issues and updates all retail G5 models, we will revisit this in future reviews of retail sets we have lined up.
Overall, the LG G5 is a big step up in colour volume and HDR brightness performance that brings it much more in line with the competition from QD-OLED in those terms. The video processing remains some of the best available on the market and pushes Sony yet again this year. Even with the small issues highlighted, the G5 is a big step up in all other areas of image quality and comes highly recommended.
Join the discussion by leaving us your thoughts in the comments section below.

item.title: Subwoofers Explained: Everything You Need To Know
item.description:

item.title: Building Cinema Rooms for Children's Hospices: Together for Cinema
item.description:
In this video, AVForums editor Phil Hinton interviews Ian Morrish, the founder of Together for Cinema. This remarkable organisation is dedicated to transforming lives by designing and installing state-of-the-art home cinema rooms within children’s hospices and other suitable venues throughout the UK. These specially crafted entertainment spaces not only serve as a haven for children and young adults facing serious health challenges but also provide a much-needed refuge for their families, caregivers, staff, and volunteers while also fostering a sense of community and togetherness.
Together for Cinema is also committed to sustainability and accessibility; they locate loving homes for outdated, secondhand, and B-stock audiovisual equipment. By doing so, they ensure that facilities, which often operate on tight budgets and struggle to afford modern entertainment options, are equipped with the means to create enjoyable experiences for their young patients and visitors. Through their efforts, Together for Cinema is making a significant impact, bringing joy and comfort to those in need and enriching their lives with the magic of cinema.
Visit the website - https://www.togetherforcinema.co.uk/

item.title: What Makes The 2025 LG G5 Flagship TV So Special
item.description:
LG held a hands-on event at Dolby HQ in London to introduce the new LG G5 Flagship Primary RGB Tandem OLED TV, along with the C5 OLED and QNED85 + QNED93 Mini LED TVs. In this video, we take a closer look at the TVs and their new features including the Filmmaker Mode Ambient setting that adjusts the TV's brightness depending on your room lighting so you can still get the creator's intent in a bright or dark room. There is also a new Gamma setting that allows easier adjustment for the room lighting and set-up.
James Thomas from LG UK also presents a tour of the new TVs and explains some of the features to us.

item.title: Philips OLED+959 Ambilight TV Review - A Dazzling Flagship TV!
item.description:
AVForums Editor Phil Hinton reviews the latest Flagship TV from Philips - The OLED+959. Read the full review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/philips-65-inch-oled-959-ambilight-tv-review.22264/
The Philips OLED+959 is an excellent flagship TV that offers something for everyone. If you want image accuracy and to view content as it was mastered and intended to be seen, the OLED+959 is excellent in this regard with superb greyscale and colour reproduction. The use of the META 2.0 MLA (Micro Lens Array) panel adds superb peak brightness capabilities and bright room viewing performance, with the 8th Gen P5 AI Dual Engine Processor adding in the video processing smarts.
And suppose you don't care for the director’s intent or want a bright and vivid image with smooth motion. In that case, the Crystal Clear picture preset is one of the most balanced ‘Vivid” settings available on the market, where Philips has tried to keep the image bright and colourful, but without going over the top with neon colours and blown highlights. The image is sharp, detailed and natural-looking to a degree that many mainstream users will be very happy using it.
Image quality with Filmmaker Mode SDR and HDR is very good indeed and we saw no major issues that concerned us in our time testing the set. There is the occasional instance of image posterisation with tricky content and some minor overshoot in the blacks, but the vast majority of viewers will never notice this and it is also very much content-dependent. Overall, the image quality on offer with the new Dual Engine processing and MLA 2.0 panel is excellent.
The audio performance from the Bowers & Wilkins 5.1.2 102W audio system is also superb with weight and scale added to a large and wide soundstage, which beats many standalone soundbars for audio fidelity and quality. Using 18 drivers in total across the front, side and top of the set, it fits in with the design of the OLED+959 adding a real sense of cinematic flair with images and sound that bring content to life with authority, even if the soundstage is mostly front-heavy with little in the way of surround effects.
Adding further immersion is the brand-new Ambilight Plus system. Building on 20 years of experience with the Ambilight technology, the new system uses 192 lighting zones with lenses that allow superb gradational resolution to colours and movement that adds more realistic effects to follow what is happening onscreen. And for purists, there is also a bias light setting that can be calibrated to the room for serious movie watching in dim surroundings without your eyes feeling tired.
Gaming is also another huge area of the market and Philips has listened to gamers when putting together its latest game bar and games mode. With game mode engaged on the two HDMI 2.1 (48Gbps) ports you get Dolby Vision gaming on Xbox, 4K/144, 4K120, VRR, ALLM and input lag of 14.6ms at 4K/60 and 6.5ms at 1080/120.
The only slight negative we can find with the OLED+959 is the use of Google TV for its smart system and the lack of catch-up terrestrial services for UK channels. This can be resolved by adding an external stick or streamer, but it would have rounded off the package nicely if the smart TV system was a little more capable for UK users.

media:group.media:title: Philips OLED+959 Ambilight TV Review - A Dazzling Flagship TV!
media:group.media:description:
AVForums Editor Phil Hinton reviews the latest Flagship TV from Philips - The OLED+959. Read the full review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/philips-65-inch-oled-959-ambilight-tv-review.22264/
The Philips OLED+959 is an excellent flagship TV that offers something for everyone. If you want image accuracy and to view content as it was mastered and intended to be seen, the OLED+959 is excellent in this regard with superb greyscale and colour reproduction. The use of the META 2.0 MLA (Micro Lens Array) panel adds superb peak brightness capabilities and bright room viewing performance, with the 8th Gen P5 AI Dual Engine Processor adding in the video processing smarts.
And suppose you don't care for the director’s intent or want a bright and vivid image with smooth motion. In that case, the Crystal Clear picture preset is one of the most balanced ‘Vivid” settings available on the market, where Philips has tried to keep the image bright and colourful, but without going over the top with neon colours and blown highlights. The image is sharp, detailed and natural-looking to a degree that many mainstream users will be very happy using it.
Image quality with Filmmaker Mode SDR and HDR is very good indeed and we saw no major issues that concerned us in our time testing the set. There is the occasional instance of image posterisation with tricky content and some minor overshoot in the blacks, but the vast majority of viewers will never notice this and it is also very much content-dependent. Overall, the image quality on offer with the new Dual Engine processing and MLA 2.0 panel is excellent.
The audio performance from the Bowers & Wilkins 5.1.2 102W audio system is also superb with weight and scale added to a large and wide soundstage, which beats many standalone soundbars for audio fidelity and quality. Using 18 drivers in total across the front, side and top of the set, it fits in with the design of the OLED+959 adding a real sense of cinematic flair with images and sound that bring content to life with authority, even if the soundstage is mostly front-heavy with little in the way of surround effects.
Adding further immersion is the brand-new Ambilight Plus system. Building on 20 years of experience with the Ambilight technology, the new system uses 192 lighting zones with lenses that allow superb gradational resolution to colours and movement that adds more realistic effects to follow what is happening onscreen. And for purists, there is also a bias light setting that can be calibrated to the room for serious movie watching in dim surroundings without your eyes feeling tired.
Gaming is also another huge area of the market and Philips has listened to gamers when putting together its latest game bar and games mode. With game mode engaged on the two HDMI 2.1 (48Gbps) ports you get Dolby Vision gaming on Xbox, 4K/144, 4K120, VRR, ALLM and input lag of 14.6ms at 4K/60 and 6.5ms at 1080/120.
The only slight negative we can find with the OLED+959 is the use of Google TV for its smart system and the lack of catch-up terrestrial services for UK channels. This can be resolved by adding an external stick or streamer, but it would have rounded off the package nicely if the smart TV system was a little more capable for UK users.
*The good* Accurate SDR and HDR image quality with excellent peak brightness capabilities Ambilight Plus is brilliant All HDR and sound formats supported Excellent audio quality Excellent build quality and unusual design
*The not so good* No full UK terrestrial catch-up service support on Google TV Pedestal stand can lead to cabling and source placement issues Ambilight Plus is only three-sided (top and sides)

item.title: Box Office DISASTERS: What Are The Worst Movie FLOPS Of 2024?
item.description:
Which movies have flopped hard so far this year? We look at 2024’s disappointments including some surprise underperformers and ask why some films look great on paper but just don’t capture the audience's interest… and others just plain suck!
Plus the guys select their top ten cinema and streaming titles for the month along with the best discs to help you with your purchasing choices for this month.
Presented by Cas Harlow, Mark Costello and Simon Crust.
00:02:03 - Recommended titles to watch at the cinema or on streaming for October 2024
*Best Titles* Joker 2 (Cinemas) 5/10 Walking Dead Daryl Dixon Book of Carol (Sky) 6/10 Citadel: Diana (Amazon) 7/10 Strange Darling (Cinemas) 7/10 Woman of the Hour (Netflix) 7/10 The Shadow Strays (Netflix) 8/10 Nobody Wants This (Netflix) 8/10 Shrinking Season 2 (Apple) 8/10 Smile 2 (Cinemas) 8/10 The Wild Robot (Cinemas) 10/10
00:13:30 - Recommended disc releases for October 2024
*Best Discs* American Pie (88 Films) 6/10 Air America (Studiocanal) 8/10 Twisters (Warner) 8/10 Late Night with the Devil (Second Sight) 8/10 A Nightmare on Elm Street (Warner) 8/10 An Inspector Calls (Studiocanal) 9/10 Night of the Living Dead (Criterion) 9/10 Trick 'r Treat (Arrow) 9/10 The African Queen (Studiocanal) 10/10 The Exorcist III (Arrow) 9/10
00:31:05 - Recommended streaming articles 00:36:26 - Worst movie flops of 2024
*Worst Movie Flops* Borderlands Our verdict: 5/10 $110–120M Budget (Calculated Breakeven: $275–300M) $33M Box Office. Loss $20–30M
The Fall Guy Our verdict: 7/10 $125–150M Budget (Reported Breakeven: $275–300M) $181M Box Office. Loss $50–60M
Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga Our verdict: 9/10 $168M Budget (Reported Breakeven: $350–375M) $174M Box Office. Loss $75–95M
Horizon: An American Saga - Chapter 1 Our verdict: 7/10 $50M Budget (Calculated Breakeven: $125M) $38M Box Office. Loss $80+M
The Crow (2024) Our verdict: 4/10 $50M Budget (Calculated Breakeven: $125M) $23M Box Office. Loss $100+M
Madame Web Our verdict: 4/10 $100M Budget (Calculated Breakeven: £250M) $100M Box Office. Loss $100+M
Joker: Folie A Deux Our verdict: 5/10 $200M Budget (Reported Breakeven: $375–450M) $190M Box Office. Loss $150–200M
Fly Me to the Moon (Apple TV+) Our verdict: 6/10 $100M Budget (Calculated Breakeven: $250M) $42M Box Office. Loss $200+M
Argylle (Apple TV+) Our verdict: 6/10 $200M Budget (Reported Breakeven: $500M) $96M Box Office. Loss $400+M
Megalopolis $120M Budget (Calculated Breakeven: $300M) $11M Box Office. Loss $250+M
Note: ALL figures are estimates. Break-even is approx 2.5 the budget of any given film. This includes the total cost of the film x 1.5 (for marketing) + 60% approx Box Office yield (averaging across domestic/int territories)

item.title: Buying Audio Gear in 2024: Are Hi-Fi Dealers Still RELEVANT?
item.description:
The AVForums Podcast is back on the main channel! From October 2024 you can find all of our Podcast episodes every Monday at 7pm.
We look at the role bricks and mortar Hi-Fi dealers and outlets play in the two channel audio buying landscape in 2024. Do you really need to demo prospective gear in person when there’s a host of YouTube Videos available? What value can a dealer add to the purchasing experience? Plus, do special edition products drive sales? We tackle these questions and more.
We also give you the lowdown on the upcoming sophomore Newcastle Audio Show, a collaboration between AVForums and Peter Tyson from 1st-3rd Nov 2024 which will see Hi-Fi demos, brand new product launches, competitions and the chance to question representatives from some of the most prestigious audio companies in the world.
Presented by Phil Hilton with Ed Selley and guest Danny Blake from Peter Tyson
*Podcast Resources* Peter Tyson and AVForums Hi-Fi Show 1-3rd Nov 2024 - https://www.avforums.com/news/newcastle-audio-show-01-03-november-2024.22128/

item.title: Panasonic Z95A OLED TV Review: Back in the USA!
item.description:
The Panasonic Z95A is the flagship OLED TV for 2024 and it is also now available to buy in the US, the first time a Panasonic TV has been available in that country for over a decade! So is it any good? AVForums Editor Phil Hinton gives you his full in-depth review.
Read the review at AVForums - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/panasonic-z95a-tv-65z95a-4k-oled-tv-review.22079/
I have spent the last few weeks living with the Panasonic Z95A and it is the type of flagship OLED TV you would expect from the manufacturer. Plus, in a not-too-surprising move following the Z95A taking pride of place on the Panasonic CES stand this year, it is also now available to buy in the US, after a break of 10 years from that market.
The latest MLA (Micro Lens Array) technology added to the proprietary heat sinks unique to Panasonic, gives the Z95A superb HDR10, HDR10+ and Dolby Vision brightness capabilities which match, or in some cases better, the 2024 flagship competition. Peak brightness in the most accurate Filmmaker mode measures in at 1539 nits on an industry-standard 10% window and 205 nits at 100% coverage. Plus, the now famous Panasonic cinematic image quality shines through yet again, offering stunning blacks, and superb shadow details adding real depth and detail to SDR and HDR images.
Gaming is also very good with two HDMI 2.1 ports (48Gbps) an improved game bar and the accurate True Game picture mode adds up to a very good gaming TV experience that should keep most users happy. Plus, we get Dolby Vision HDR gaming up to 120Hz and PC gamers can also take advantage of the 144Hz capabilities of the panel.
The switch to Fire TV for the OS system is also a good one with a large selection of apps and features, along with the Freely TV service due to be added soon. It feels slick, fast and stable with a large selection of on-demand and TV services across most of the major platforms out there.
It’s not perfect with a few niggles we would like to see fixed with a firmware update for calibration and accuracy, but in all other areas, the Panasonic Z95A lives up to its flagship status and comes Highly Recommended.
*The good* Superb cinematic image quality with SDR & HDR content Superb black levels and shadow detail retrieval True game picture mode, game bar and decent gaming features Very good sound quality
*The not so good* Only two 48Gbps HDMI 2.1 ports with eARC using one Out of the Box accuracy could be slightly better Menu system covers too much image area for calibration

item.title: Hisense U8N TV Review: The BEST Hisense Mini LED TV?
item.description:
We review the latest flagship ULED TV from Hisense, the U8N. Is this the best Mini LED TV Hisense has made? AVForums Editor Phil Hinton gives you the full details in our video review and read the full written review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/hisense-u8n-65u8nqtuk-4k-uled-review.21915/
The Hisense U8N is the best mini LED TV we have seen from the company with a continued improvement in picture quality since last year’s model. We noted improved HDR10 tone mapping with content up to 1000 nits with no obvious signs of clipping or PQ EOTF over brightening and it now feels like a more significantly polished product.
It’s not perfect as we still get the drawbacks of LCD technology with some instances of clouding and dirty screen effect, and blacks are not entirely well controlled throughout. This is more noticeable in dark viewing conditions so, when used in a brightly lit room, many of these negatives are well mitigated in most instances.
Out of the box, in Filmmaker Mode, we found that colour accuracy with SDR and HDR is very good with excellent gradational performance, natural-looking colours and lifelike skin tones. Images are also bright enough for this TV to excel in a well-lit living room environment.
Gaming is also strong with two HDMI 2.1 (48Gbps) ports supporting 4K/144Hz for PC gaming, 4K/120Hz gaming in Dolby Vision thanks to the use of the new Pentonic SOC, a games menu bar and impressive input lag. The U8N may even make our round up of Best Gaming TVs for 2024.
Overall, the Hisense U8N makes a compelling case for the mass market consumer looking for a well-rounded bright room TV and it comes recommended.

item.title: A TV Soundbar, An Expensive HiFi Or BOTH? Canvas Speaker Review
item.description:
The Canvas HiFi Speaker system is a unique and niche product that offers superb Hi-Fi stereo sound in a speaker that fits neatly under your existing 55-inch and larger TV set. But is it a soundbar or a premium Hi-Fi speaker?
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/canvas-hifi-speaker-system-review.21890/
The Canvas does what it says on the tin with exceptional audio performance for those looking for a superb stereo solution that fits within a well-designed living space. It has excellent build quality and design options that make it incredibly flexible within any interior design. The BACCH 3D processing offers an amazing stereo separation and sound stage with stunning clarity, detail and bass weight.
It is not designed to replace a 7.2.4 Dolby Atmos theatre system or soundbar and anyone looking for that kind of solution will need to look elsewhere. The Canvas is a niche product at a relatively high price point, but it certainly offers up the kind of performance you would expect from such a product, and for those looking for such a solution, it comes highly recommended.
*The good* Huge soundstage with excellent musicality and tight bass response Excellent clarity and separation with BACCH 3D processing Superb build quality and interior design features Excellent flexibility of sources It fits flush with most TV designs 55-inch and over
*The not so good* Fits a somewhat niche use case Expensive

item.title: Hisense U7N Mini LED Review - Good Value For Money TV?
item.description:
In this in-depth TV review, we take a closer look at the Hisense U7N to see if it's worth the investment. Watch to find out if this TV offers good value for money! The Hisense U7N has very good performance within its market segment and is best suited to rooms with ambient light. It is not a TV designed for critical movie watching in the dark, but for all other uses, it offers excellent features and image quality for those looking for a living room workhorse.
In terms of features, the U7N has you well covered with all current HDR formats supported including Dolby Vision IQ. There are also two HDMI 2.1 (48Gbps) inputs for gamers with support for 144Hz VRR, Game Pro Mode and AMD Freesync compatibility along with the latest Mini LED Pro backlight, updated Hi-View Engine Pro processor with advanced AI and a Freely tuner built-in.
The Hisense U7N offers bright and vivid images for the typical living room as well as a good degree of accuracy to greyscale and colour, along with excellent gaming features, HDR support and its VIDAA smart TV system and will appeal to the mass market audience. It is a little expensive when compared to the direct competition, but I still think it is good value for money in the right use case and as such it comes recommended.

item.title: HiFi Rose RA280 Amplifier Review: Hefty Power On Tap
item.description:
Looking for a powerful amplifier? Check out this review of the HiFi Rose RA280 Amplifier by our editor, Ed Selley. Find out if this amplifier has the power you need for your audio setup!
The RA280 might not be the obvious choice at the price point but neither that, nor the quirky looks, should distract you from what is an extremely talented amplifier and one that will work in a variety of systems extremely effectively. HiFi Rose's wholly unique approach to audio is far more than bluster; it's really beginning to impress.
I wasn’t completely sure what to expect when I unboxed the RA280. I imagined it would be a competent enough device but I genuinely wasn’t expecting what actually resulted. This is a device that charms and delights from the get go. Behind the unique but actually very usable design is a combination of enormous headroom and beguiling presentation that appealed from the outset and only became more engaging the more I used it. This is far more than a partner to the Rose streamers. For anyone with their digital sources sorted, this is a beautifully realised take on a three-grand amplifier and one that comes Highly Recommended.
*Pros* Combines volcanic power with sweetness and tonal realism Excellent phono stage Superbly made
*Cons* Quirky volume control No headphone socket or digital board Looks will divide opinion

item.title: Why The Bowers & Wilkins 702 S3 Signature is a Must-Have
item.description:
Ed Selley reviews the Bowers & Wilkins 702 S3 Signature Floor Standing Speakers, priced at £7000. You can read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/bowers-wilkins-702-s3-signature-speaker-review.21755/
The 702 S3 Signature doesn't quite hit the heights of the 805 but we're still talking degrees of excellence meaning that it needs to be seen as one of the best sub £10k speaker options on the market. The detail tweaks make a good speaker that bit better and the gorgeous finishes make it feel more expensive than it is. Bowers' ongoing Signature program continues to deliver the goods.
*Pros* Big, confident and engaging sound Beautifully made and finished Relatively easy to drive and place
*Cons* Some key rivals are fractionally more fun A bit of a pig to unbox and move around The basic model is very good too...

item.title: LG C4 OLED TV Review: EXPLOSIVE Performance?
item.description:
The LG C4 OLED Evo TV is the sweet spot in the 2024 line-up offering excellent all-round performance for movies, TV shows, Smart TV and Gaming! We give you our video review.
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/lg-c4-oled65c4-4k-oled-tv-review.21805/
The C-series is the most important part of the OLED TV line-up for LG as it is the sweet spot for price, features and performance with an excellent all-round appeal. With its Alpha9 AI Processor 4K Gen 7 chip and the latest OLED EX panel with Brightness Booster, we do see a step up in overall image performance, with brighter full screen and specular highlight details and colours that look natural, accurate and rich with lifelike skin tones. As you would expect, the Filmmaker Mode is incredibly accurate out of the box to the industry standards so you can see films and TV shows as they were mastered and intended to be seen.
Gaming is also a strong point with 4K/144Hz, 4K/120Hz with Dolby Vision, NVIDIA G-Sync, AMD FreeSync Premium, and VRR as well as the Game Optimizer and dashboard. Input lag is also superb with 4K/60 measured at 9.2ms and 120Hz at 4.7ms, so a place on our Best Gaming TVs is a possibility.
Overall, with a cinematic sheen to film content, very good HDR peak brightness and tone mapping capabilities, mixed with superb gaming features and a strong WebOS 24 line-up of features and apps, the C4 offers the best of what LG has to offer at the mid-range point. It gets a Highly Recommended.

item.title: World's Smallest OLED TV With Built-In Soundbar? Panasonic OLED & Mini LED TVs launched!
item.description:
Panasonic launched their full TV line-up for 2024 including new OLED, Mini LED and LED LCD models. The flagship will be the Z95A OLED with MLA and META 2.0 for increased brightness along with the HCX Pro AI II processor. Next is the 77-inch Z93A with the same built-in Dolby Atmos sound system.
Further models include Z90A the World's smallest OLED TV with a built-in soundbar at 42-inch and 48-inch screen sizes. The Z90A will be available in 42, 48, 55 and 65-inch sizes, with the larger two options using Master OLED Pro technology. All models boast the same upgraded HCX Pro AI Processor MKII as those flagship models, along with Game Mode Extreme should you have a set-up that can make good use of its 144Hz refresh rates.
The Z85A will be available in 55 and 65-inch versions, with similar “advanced gaming features” topping out at 120Hz. It also sports that new HCX Pro AI Processor MKII with its associated perks including improved upscaling and noise reduction, with the new 4K Fine Remaster Engine designed to ensure that “every scene is displayed with the utmost precision and naturalism”, with a particular nod towards streaming content. The Z80A will be using an older HCX Processor, but will still come with all the trimmings of that Fire TV set-up and Panasonic’s own Premium TV offerings, and at a more budget-friendly price point.
Topping Panasonic’s LED line-up will be the W95A MiniLED, with 55, 65, and 75-inch models on the way. It echoes the Z90A in terms of the MKII processor and 144Hz refresh rates, along with the other top-tier features. The same applies to the W90A, which comes with Full Array LED backlighting for its 43, 50, 55, and 65-inch selection – with the same four sizes on offer for the W80A and W60A TVs. The W60A does look to mark something of an outlier with a TiVo operating system in place, as Panasonic’s line-up continues beyond those ‘high-end’ models that are part of the new Amazon/Fire TV partnership.
If you’re looking for something smaller (and cheaper) the S55/50 and S45/40 models will offer some 24, 32 and 40-inch options, with the former still boasting that Fire TV OS and the latter providing a second TiVo solution. You’ll also find a further 24 and 32-inch option courtesy of the N30, but that HD LED will be lacking the higher-end smart TV features.
Read the news story here - https://www.avforums.com/news/panasonic-confirms-its-full-4k-oled-and-led-premium-tv-line-up.21794/

item.title: AVForums & Peter Tyson Hi-Fi Show: Big Brands on Demo
item.description:
Retailer Peter Tyson joined forces with AVForums for a North East England Hi-Fi show where the public had free entry to hear some of the very best Hi-Fi systems on the planet. The entire net value of the systems listened to was well over £1M.
It was a no-pressure enthusiast-based event in association with AVForums where the public had the opportunity to listen to a wide selection of audio systems and choose their demo material. There were three dedicated demo rooms with acoustic treatments and a further six systems set up across the upstairs speaker gallery with many smaller Hi-Fi systems on demo in the showroom downstairs.
Some of the systems on show included the brand new Bowers & Wilkins 700 S3 Signature speakers with Linn Selekt. Bowers & Wilkins 803 partnered with Marantz PM10 & SA10 with a premium turntable. Plus, there were systems featuring Bowers & Wilkins 801 D4 Signatures, Naim Statement, Mcintosh, Sonus faber, Linn and more...
Would you like to attend a similar AVForums event in the future? Let us know in the comments below.

item.title: Don't Buy the Acoustic Energy Corinium Speaker Until You Watch This!
item.description:
The Acoustic Energy Corinium speaker is a tremendous Hi-Fi achievement and has skills and abilities that are comfortably in advance of any speaker product we've seen from the company before and finished to an exceptional standard. When you need it to be though, it's as joyous and engaging as an Acoustic Energy floor-standing speaker should be.
Join our Hi-Fi Editor Ed Selley as he takes you through the pros and cons of these new flagship high-end Hi-Fi speakers.
00:00 - Start 00:19 - Intro 00:41 - What is a Corinium? 01:15 - The History of the Corinium Speaker and AE1 03:12 - The materials used in the drivers 04:20 - The performance of the drivers and set-up 05:33 - Design, cabinet and room placement 07:18 - Price point 08:07 - Sound quality 10:00 - Conclusion 11:37 - Wrap up 12:03 - List of Patrons
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/acoustic-energy-corinium-loudpeaker-review.21682/
The Acoustic Energy Corinium is a 3.5 way floorstanding speaker and the new flagship of the Acoustic Energy range. As it stands, it is the only speaker of this type that the company intends to make and it represents a significant increase in cost over the AE520 which has been the range topper so far. It even gains a name instead of a number; the Roman name for what is now Cirencester near where Acoustic Energy is based.
This increase in cost brings with it a significant increase in expectations too. A six-grand speaker is realistically the start of what can be described as the high-end. It represents an investment that requires thought and no little bravery and with that comes a tendency to be more risk-averse. It’s all very well telling somebody else to try an all-new arrival but when it comes to your hard-earned, you’re probably going with the known quantities. For the Corinium to be in with a shout of winning you over it needs to be very good indeed.
It also needs to meet a challenge more specific to Acoustic Energy. This is a company with a formidable reputation for small speakers over and above anything else. The Corinium is actually fractionally shorter than the AE520 but it is by most judgements a large speaker. How does the company leverage its small speaker excellence into making something a bit heftier and does the end result work? It’s time to find out.

It even gains a name instead of a number; the Roman name for what is now Cirencester near where Acoustic Energy is based.
This increase in cost brings with it a significant increase in expectations too. A six-grand speaker is realistically the start of what can be described as the high-end. It represents an investment that requires thought and no little bravery and with that comes a tendency to be more risk-averse. It’s all very well telling somebody else to try an all-new arrival but when it comes to your hard-earned, you’re probably going with the known quantities. For the Corinium to be in with a shout of winning you over it needs to be very good indeed.
It also needs to meet a challenge more specific to Acoustic Energy. This is a company with a formidable reputation for small speakers over and above anything else. The Corinium is actually fractionally shorter than the AE520 but it is by most judgements a large speaker. How does the company leverage its small speaker excellence into making something a bit heftier and does the end result work? It’s time to find out.

item.title: Sony BRAVIA 9 Mini LED TV: The Best HDR TV EVER?
item.description:
The Sony BRAVIA 9 Mini LED TV was launched at Sony Pictures Studios back in March with the Sony BRAVIA 8 OLED and BRAVIA 7 Mini LED also breaking cover. As well as the TVs there are also BRAVIA Theatre products including new soundbars and a Home Theatre system. Sony is not removing OLED TVs from their line-up, the A95L continues for another year.
Read our full in-depth article - https://www.avforums.com/news/sony-bravia-9-bravia-8-and-bravia-7-tvs-released-at-sony-pictures-la.21721/
Sony has finally revealed the BRAVIA 9 TV model number for the 2024 flagship, based on the backlight demonstrations that were given in Tokyo late last year to a small group of journalists and again in closed-door demonstrations at CES in January. I was so impressed at the prototype demo I received at CES that we gave Sony a ‘Best of CES’ award on the spot. To finally see the product in person and with a model number was interesting and a good opportunity to see some content playing without half of the screen missing as was the case in the earlier demos.
While Sony will never divulge figures for backlight zones, the number of Mini-LEDs used or the peak brightness nit values, the BRAVIA 9 is designed to be the brightest set it has ever produced based on technology and know-how from the company's professional grading monitors.
The latest grading model, the 31-inch BVM-HX3110 is capable of achieving 4,000 nits peak brightness and in demonstrations, it is incredibly impressive with HDR content looking natural and life-like, as intended. The sun in the sky behind clouds has stunning peak highlight detail, mixed with superb mid-tones and blacks, that give the image depth and realism.
The technology used by Sony to achieve this peak brightness and accuracy with HDR content at 4,000 nits is trickling down to the consumer BRAVIA 9 which will be capable of achieving at least 3,000 nits peak with some degree of accuracy for HDR content. Sony has decided to use the BRAVIA branding to rename its TV and Home AV products to make it easier for consumers to choose and combine products within the range and understand the levels that the products perform in. By simplifying the naming convention the company hopes that consumers can easily identify the products that will suit them most within the line-up and be able to understand the product hierarchy easily. This change will take some time to work through for the entire range as some models will be staying around for a while with the older model naming structure.
Those screens remaining in the line-up for most of 2024 are the A95L QD-OLED, A90K WRGB OLED, X90L, X85L, X80L, X75WL and W800 LCD TVs.

item.title: LG G4 OLED Evo TV Full Review: It's a Winner!
item.description:
We review the LG G4 OLED Evo TV - the latest flagship Gallery series model which now offers not only a wall mount version but the 55 and 65-inch version can be bought with a tabletop stand that holds the panel vertically. It features MLA+ and META Technology 2.0 that increase brightness and HDR performance, but the real star of the show is the new Alpha 11 AI Processor.

Read our in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/lg-g4-oled65g4-oled-evo-tv-review.21669/
The LG G4 is still the OLED TV to beat in 2024, offering superbly accurate picture quality for film fans with Dolby Vision, HDR10 and HLG high dynamic range formats. There are excellent smart TV capabilities with WebOS 24 once again proving to be the easiest system to use thanks to a simple design and superb features.
Gamers get 144Hz capabilities along with 4K/120Hz (including Dolby Vision), Game Optimiser mode including ALLM switching, dark room mode, NVIDIA G-Sync (144Hz validated) and AMD Freesync Premium as well as four full bandwidth HDMI 2.1 inputs. It is an all-in-one OLED TV for the whole family offering excellent features for all use cases. It wouldn't be surprising to see it make an appearance on our Best Gaming TV rundown in relatively short order.
The newly added features are worthwhile thanks to the powerful Alpha 11 AI processor, with excellent sharpness to the image thanks to AI Director processing using contrast and brightness techniques to make edges and details look sharp and natural, with no signs of forced edge enhancement and colours looking accurate and natural. You also have the option to tailor your peak highlight detail roll-off with 1000, 4000 and 10,000 nit mastered content using the HDR Professional mode. And with HDR the G4 uses the latest LG Display Micro Lens Array (MLA+) panel and updated Meta Technology 2.0 Booster processing. This combined with the new Alpha 11 AI processor ups the peak highlight capabilities of the TV.
I have no hesitation in saying the LG G4 is the Best-in-Class OLED TV for 2024 and continues to offer the best all-in-one use case for the whole family.

It is an all-in-one OLED TV for the whole family offering excellent features for all use cases. It wouldn't be surprising to see it make an appearance on our Best Gaming TV rundown in relatively short order.
The newly added features are worthwhile thanks to the powerful Alpha 11 AI processor, with excellent sharpness to the image thanks to AI Director processing using contrast and brightness techniques to make edges and details look sharp and natural, with no signs of forced edge enhancement and colours looking accurate and natural. You also have the option to tailor your peak highlight detail roll-off with 1000, 4000 and 10,000 nit mastered content using the HDR Professional mode. And with HDR the G4 uses the latest LG Display Micro Lens Array (MLA+) panel and updated Meta Technology 2.0 Booster processing. This combined with the new Alpha 11 AI processor ups the peak highlight capabilities of the TV.
I have no hesitation in saying the LG G4 is the Best-in-Class OLED TV for 2024 and continues to offer the best all-in-one use case for the whole family.

item.title: Technics SL-1200GR2 Turntable Review - An Audiophile Deck?
item.description:
The legendary Technics SL-1200 turntable is back and better than ever! In this review, we take a closer look at the brand-new SL-1200GR2 and see how it measures up to its predecessors.
If you're a DJ, audiophile, or just a fan of vinyl, this review is a must-watch. We'll cover all the features of this high-end direct drive turntable and give you our honest opinion on its performance. Spoiler alert: is it a potential game-changer for the hi-fi market!
AVForums Hi-Fi editor Ed Selley takes a look to see what improvements have been made over the original GR model from 2016.
One of the big new features of the Technics SL-1200GR2 is the use of ΔΣ-Drive (Delta Sigma Drive) to control the speed of the direct drive motor to give the Turntable accurate pitch and speed, but also kill any unwanted vibrations or noise that could be transmitted to the cartridge pick up, giving you a cleaner sound.
With its universal design and high-fidelity sound, the Technics SL-1200GR2 is a must-have for any vinyl enthusiast. Whether you're a professional DJ or just enjoy listening to music, this turntable will take your vinyl experience to the next level. Watch this video to see why the legend has returned and is better than ever!

Also announced were the OLED+909 & OLED809 sets which also feature the new Pentonic chipset in a single chip P5 AI processor and Ambilight, with the return to four sides on the OLED+909.
Read the full details - https://www.avforums.com/news/philips-unveils-its-new-oled-959-and-oled-909-tvs.21507/

item.title: MASSIVE 115 Inch QD Mini LED TV from TCL! - CES 2024
item.description:

item.title: CES 2024: Samsung 42 & 48 Inch S90D, and 65 inch S85D LG based OLED TVs, PLUS, 3rd Gen QD OLED S95D
item.description:
We visit the Samsung First Look event at CES 2024 to see the new S85D, S90D and S95D OLED TVs. The 3rd Gen QD OLED S95D will be available in 55, 65 and 77-inch screen sizes and offers a new anti-glare screen surface. The more interesting story, certainly from what we saw in person is the 65-inch S85D and 42-inch and 48-inch S90D models which appear to use LG Display WRGB (WOLED) panels and not Samsung display-produced QD OLEDs.

item.title: ⭐ Philips OLED908 TV & Musical Fidelity A1 amp reviews + a look at two home cinema speaker packages
item.description:

item.title: Panasonic's First Mini LED & Return To High End LCD: Panasonic MX950 Review
item.description:
Panasonic returns to the high-end LCD fold with their first Mini LED TV, the MX950. Read the full review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/panasonic-mx950-tx-55mx950b-4k-mini-led-tv-review.21270/
00:00 - Intro 00:27 - What is the MX950? 01:37 - Quick Verdict 03:28 - Full Review 08:06 - Final Verdict
The Panasonic MX950 is an excellent MiniLED model that will fulfil the role of living room workhorse for many consumers. It is not a screen that should be used for critical movie watching in dark surroundings, but anyone looking for a Panasonic model for that use will undoubtedly find what they're looking for with the MZ OLED models.
The MX950 is also not a replacement for the superb DX902 model from 2016 that won many fans over for its superb FALD backlight and cinematic images.
No, the MX950 is a solid Mini LED-equipped LCD TV that offers the type of image quality you expect from Panasonic, aimed at the mass market consumer looking for a bright set for living room use with gaming, sports and the occasional movie with the lights on.
There are two HDMI 2.1 (40Gbps) inputs with support for 4K/120 HDR10 gaming, VRR, ALLM and eARC, plus the True Game mode for excellent gaming image quality to the standards. While it does also feature some of the downsides associated with Mini LED LCD TVs, such as haloing, blooming and poor viewing angles, used in the bright room and watching directly onto the set, the image quality is very good for this sector of the market. It comes recommended.
*The good* Very good bright room image quality and accuracy Support for all HDR formats True game picture mode, game bar and decent gaming features Good sound quality
*The not so good* Only two 40Gbps HDMI 2.1 ports with eARC using one Poor viewing angles and haloing around bright objects Blacks are weak in dim room viewing and black bars are not black

item.title: Panasonic MZ1500 Review - No Longer The Enthusiast's Choice?
item.description:
Panasonic has changed the 1500 model so it no longer features the flagship panel minus the Dolby Atmos audio system. The MZ1500 for 2023 offers last year's panel without MLA and a new soundbar that many enthusiasts will not want. So what gives?
00:00 - Intro 00:14 - What is the MZ1500? 02:12 - MZ1500 Quick Verdict 03:20 - MZ1500 Full Review 08:12 - MZ1500 Final Verdict
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/panasonic-mz1500-tx-55mz1500b-4k-oled-tv-review.21269/
Join the discussion - https://www.avforums.com/threads/panasonic-mz1500-tx-55mz1500b-4k-oled-tv-review-comments.2475524/
Watch the best settings video - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fFQtWEzgORk
The Panasonic MZ1500 is an excellent mid-tier OLED TV designed for movie fans and dark room viewing conditions. Sadly it doesn’t have the top-end MLA (Micro Lens Array) panel found in the flagship MZ2000, but it does feature the previous flagship Master OLED Pro panel with a proprietary heat sink found in last year’s models.
SDR and HDR content is accurate thanks to Filmmaker Mode out of the box, plus there is the added benefit for bright room viewing with a new light sensor and white balance adjustment that follows the creator's intent but adjusts the image to suit your environment.
Plus, there is support for HDR10, HDR10+, HDR10+Adaptive, Dolby Vision, Dolby Vision IQ and HLG (Hybrid Log-Gamma) HDR formats and gaming is well catered for with two HDMI 2.1 ports (40Gbps), an improved game bar and an accurate True Game picture mode. It’s an impressive package that sits well with competing sets at this level of the market and comes highly recommended.
*The good* Excellent cinematic SDR & HDR image quality Support for all HDR formats True game picture mode, game bar and decent gaming features Good sound quality
*The not so good* Only two 40Gbps HDMI 2.1 ports with eARC using one Some visible posterisation around bright objects Just above black dithering and some black crush noticeable
We use Portrait Displays’ Calman colour calibration software (https://www.portrait.com) a Murideo Seven Generator and a Klein K-10A meter profiled to a JETI Spectraval 1511-HiRes spectroradiometer for measurement and calibration.

item.title: The BEST TV of 2023? Sony BRAVIA XR A95L QD OLED Review
item.description:
The Sony A95L is one of the most anticipated TVs of 2023 marrying 2nd Generation QD-OLED technology, with Sony's excellent video processing and unlike the Samsung QD OLEDs, it also has Dolby Vision on board. Is this the best TV of 2023? Let's find out...
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/sony-a95l-xr-65a95l-bravia-4k-qd-oled-tv-review.21228/
This review was made possible thanks to the assistance of Peter Tyson who supplied us with a retail example of the Sony A95L as well as 55-inch LG G3 and Samsung S95C TVs for comparison. If you want to support our channel and future review videos like this, please consider your next AV purchase from https://www.petertyson.co.uk
The A95L has the full benefits of second-generation QD OLED with its stunning colour volume and decent image uniformity, added to what Sony does best with image upscaling, motion and video processing which adds up to one of the very best OLED TVs of 2023. There is no such thing as the perfect TV and that is certainly true here with some areas slightly lacking compared to its peers when it comes to gaming and only offering two HDMI 2.1 ports with eARC on one of those. Plus, this is a very expensive TV when compared to the LG G3 and Samsung S95C as all of these TVs are very close to each other in terms of picture quality. But with that said, Sony continues to push forward the QD OLED case and does so with stunning image quality, motion reproduction and image processing and is clearly a Best in Class performer.
*The good* Outstanding SDR, HDR10 and Dolby Vision accuracy and image quality Stunning video upscaling, motion and XR processing Great sound quality from Acoustic Surface Audio+ Google TV is stable and fast
*The not so good* No Filmmaker Mode AutoCal fixed to 2.2 gamma and 1D LUT Only two HDMI 2.1 (48Gbps) inputs Very expensive when compared to peers
Join the discussion at AVForums - https://www.avforums.com/threads/sony-a95l-xr-65a95l-bravia-4k-qd-oled-tv-review-comments.2473948/

media:group.media:title: The BEST TV of 2023? Sony BRAVIA XR A95L QD OLED Review
media:group.media:description:
The Sony A95L is one of the most anticipated TVs of 2023 marrying 2nd Generation QD-OLED technology, with Sony's excellent video processing and unlike the Samsung QD OLEDs, it also has Dolby Vision on board. Is this the best TV of 2023? Let's find out...
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/sony-a95l-xr-65a95l-bravia-4k-qd-oled-tv-review.21228/
This review was made possible thanks to the assistance of Peter Tyson who supplied us with a retail example of the Sony A95L as well as 55-inch LG G3 and Samsung S95C TVs for comparison. If you want to support our channel and future review videos like this, please consider your next AV purchase from https://www.petertyson.co.uk
The A95L has the full benefits of second-generation QD OLED with its stunning colour volume and decent image uniformity, added to what Sony does best with image upscaling, motion and video processing which adds up to one of the very best OLED TVs of 2023. There is no such thing as the perfect TV and that is certainly true here with some areas slightly lacking compared to its peers when it comes to gaming and only offering two HDMI 2.1 ports with eARC on one of those. Plus, this is a very expensive TV when compared to the LG G3 and Samsung S95C as all of these TVs are very close to each other in terms of picture quality. But with that said, Sony continues to push forward the QD OLED case and does so with stunning image quality, motion reproduction and image processing and is clearly a Best in Class performer.
*The good* Outstanding SDR, HDR10 and Dolby Vision accuracy and image quality Stunning video upscaling, motion and XR processing Great sound quality from Acoustic Surface Audio+ Google TV is stable and fast
*The not so good* No Filmmaker Mode AutoCal fixed to 2.2 gamma and 1D LUT Only two HDMI 2.1 (48Gbps) inputs Very expensive when compared to peers
Join the discussion at AVForums - https://www.avforums.com/threads/sony-a95l-xr-65a95l-bravia-4k-qd-oled-tv-review-comments.2473948/
We use Portrait Displays’ Calman colour calibration software (https://www.portrait.com) a Murideo Seven Generator and a Klein K-10A meter profiled to a JETI Spectraval 1511-HiRes spectroradiometer for measurement and calibration.

item.title: Hisense U8K (65U8K) 4K Mini LED TV Review - The Best Yet?
item.description:
Read the full review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/hisense-u8k-65u8k-4k-mini-led-tv-review.21167/ The Hisense U8K is a big improvement from last year’s model and is probably the best Mini LED TV we have yet seen from the company. It is not all perfect, there are some issues with clouding and dirty screen effect which is a by-product of the technology used, and we also noted raised black levels with scope film content and in comparisons.
HDR tone mapping could also be better as we see detail clipping from 600 nits with HDR10 content and only two HDMI 2.1 ports with eARC using one of those is also a potential negative for gamers. But having pointed all of those issues out, the overall performance of the U8K is very good indeed for a Mini LED TV, with excellent calibrated image accuracy, very good shadow detail retrieval and decent overall black levels. Colour accuracy with SDR and HDR is very good with excellent gradational performance, natural-looking colours and lifelike skin tones.
With very good gaming capabilities, including 4K/120Hz gaming in Dolby Vision thanks to the use of the new Pentonic SoC, a games menu bar and frame rate counter, and very good sound quality thanks to a built-in soundbar and subwoofer, the Hisense U8K offers very good performance for the money and comes *recommended*.
*The good* 1700+ nits of peak brightness available Accurate greyscale and colour with SDR and HDR once calibrated (FMM is good OOTB) Two HDMI 2.1 inputs at 48Gbps with very good gaming credentials Very good sound quality and build.
*The not-so-good* HDR10 tone mapping can clip detail higher than 600 nits Dynamic HDR tone mapping over brightens the image Some DSE, clouding and banding seen
Join the discussion at AVForums - https://www.avforums.com/threads/hisense-u8k-65u8k-4k-mini-led-tv-review-comments.2472012/
We use Portrait Displays’ Calman colour calibration software (https://www.portrait.com) a Murideo Seven Generator and a Klein K-10A meter profiled to a JETI Spectraval 1511-HiRes spectroradiometer for measurement and calibration.

item.title: Panasonic MZ2000 Micro Lens Array OLED TV Review - Highest peak brightness of all 2023 OLED TVs
item.description:
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/panasonic-mz2000-tx-55mz2000b-4k-mla-oled-tv-review.21072/
The Panasonic MZ2000 is a superb flagship OLED TV designed for movie fans and now offers the brightness benefits of MLA (Micro Lens Array) technology mixed with proprietary heat sinks to offer superb peak brightness and HDR playback.
SDR and HDR content are accurate thanks to Filmmaker Mode out of the box, plus there is the added benefit to bright room viewing of a new light sensor and white balance adjustment that follows the creator's intent but adjusts the image to suit your environment.
Peak brightness and HDR tone mapping match that of the other major flagships in 2023, with excellent HDR10, HLG and Dolby Vision playback that is incredibly bright, vivid and colourful.
Gaming is also good with two HDMI 2.1 ports (40Gbps) an improved game bar and an accurate True Game picture mode. It’s not perfect and there are a few slight niggles here and there, but overall, the Panasonic MZ2000 offers superb cinematic SDR and HDR image quality along with an excellent Dolby Atmos sound system and it certainly lives up to its flagship status.
Highly Recommended.
*The good* Superb cinematic SDR & HDR image quality Excellent brightness with superb black levels and shadow detail retrieval True game picture mode, game bar and decent gaming features Very good sound quality
*The not so good* Only two 40Gbps HDMI 2.1 ports with eARC using one Some posterisation around bright objects Some just above black dithering noticeable
Best picture settings for the MZ2000 - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2LKw6VTib7Y
Join the discussion at AVForums - https://www.avforums.com/threads/panasonic-mz2000-tx-55mz2000b-4k-mla-oled-tv-review-comments.2468160/
We use Portrait Displays’ Calman colour calibration software (https://www.portrait.com) a Murideo Seven Generator and a Klein K-10A meter profiled to a JETI Spectraval 1511-HiRes spectroradiometer for measurement and calibration.

item.title: TCL C845 Review - A huge 65-inch gaming and 2000 nits HDR screen for £1000! What's the CATCH?
item.description:
*Read the full in-depth review* - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/tcl-c845-65c845k-4k-mini-led-tv-review.21050/ The *TCL C845* is an affordable budget-level 65-inch TV that offers plenty of features and an image that is bright with plenty of punch.
The problem for movie enthusiasts is that this brightness is inaccurate and can cause the image to look washed out in dark viewing rooms. There is a lack of contrast and blacks can look milky as a result, which is unusual for a VA panel LCD TV. The reason is the local dimming algorithm adds too much brightness and gamma adjustment to SDR and HDR10 content, with some raised blacks and black bars that are not pure black. This will not be as noticeable for bright room viewing where the C845 is going to spend most of its working life. Hopefully, TCL will fix this issue with a firmware update for those looking for accurate images.
For everything else, the C845 is great value for money with very good gaming features including two full bandwidth HDMI 2.1 ports and eARC on one of the HDMI 2.0 ports so you don’t lose a 2.1 if you want to add a soundbar. As a large-screen gaming TV, it is a fantastic option giving users access to the latest features, a huge screen with very good HDR performance and fast input lag for even the most demanding of gamers. For all those reasons it gets a *Recommended* badge.
*The good* Over 2000 nits HDR peak in Movie mode Very good value for money gaming performance Two HDMI 2.1 inputs at 48Gbps and eARC on an HDMI 2.0 port Decent sound quality
*The not so good* SDR can look washed out due to an over-bright local dimming algorithm HDR tone mapping is overly bright with HDR10 Dynamic HDR tone mapping over brightening the image Some light DSE and banding seen
Join the discussion at AVForums - https://www.avforums.com/threads/tcl-c845-65c845k-4k-mini-led-tv-review-comments.2467461/
We use Portrait Displays’ Calman colour calibration software (https://www.portrait.com) a Murideo Seven Generator and a Klein K-10A meter profiled to a JETI Spectraval 1511-HiRes spectroradiometer for measurement and calibration.
