item.title: Panasonic MZ980 4K OLED TV Review - Mid-Range MOVIE Masterpiece?
item.description:
*Read the full in-depth review* - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/panasonic-mz980-tx-55mz980b-4k-oled-tv-review.21037/
The Panasonic MZ980 is yet another solid mid-range OLED TV from the company, with great features and image quality on offer. If you are a movie fan and can’t quite reach the MZ1500 or flagship MZ2000, the MZ980 offers you some of the best cinematic image quality at its market level. SDR and HDR content are accurate thanks to Filmmaker Mode out of the box, but you also have full calibration capabilities if required and the MZ980 excels with images that look realistic, cinematic and accurate. The peak brightness for HDR is not quite as bright as the higher models which have heat sinks built-in, but that doesn’t mean the HDR on the MZ980 is lacking. Indeed, superb tone mapping capabilities and very good video processing plus motion help produce compelling picture quality in this market segment. Gaming is also good with two HDMI 2.1 ports (40Gbps), an improved game bar and an accurate True Game picture mode. Overall, the Panasonic MZ980 offers an excellent entry point to a range of TVs that excel with movie content and if you’re a home cinema fan looking for a new TV at a slightly smaller screen size, you need to add this to your demo list. Recommended for film fans with dark rooms.
*The good* Excellent cinematic SDR & HDR image quality Very good black levels and shadow detail retrieval in dark room viewing True game picture mode, game bar and decent gaming features Excellent build quality
*The not so good* Only two 40Gbps HDMI 2.1 ports with eARC using one No large screen sizes at this market segment or feature level Looks a little bit expensive at launch compared to direct rivals
Join the discussion at AVForums - https://www.avforums.com/threads/panasonic-mz980-tx-55mz980b-4k-oled-tv-review-discussion.2466752/

item.title: Hisense U7K 4K Mini LED TV Review - Are Hisense still VALUE FOR MONEY?
item.description:
*Read the full in-depth review* - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/hisense-u7k-65u7k-4k-mini-led-tv-review.21014/
The Hisense U7K is an improvement over last year’s models and that is the result of the company listening to feedback and fixing the items that needed to be addressed. As such, the U7K you buy in the UK matches the same TVs with that model number in other countries. Well done to Hisense for doing that and continuing to improve its products for end users. The U7K offers up fantastic features with all HDR formats supported and two full bandwidth HDMI 2.1 ports with excellent gaming credentials to boot. Image quality is a step up on last year with better accuracy, black levels and shadow detail retrieval. HDR is also good, but it does lack overall brightness and contrast when compared to rivals and the tone mapping clips highlight detail over 600 nits, rather than matching and adapting to the mastering monitor metadata. But, with good smart TV execution, very good bright room images, excellent gaming features and solid build quality, the U7K offers many things for a mass market audience. It is a little expensive when compared to direct competition, but you still get a lot of screen real estate for the money! For all those reasons it gets a Recommended badge.
*The good* Accurate greyscale and colour with SDR and HDR in Filmmaker Mode Two HDMI 2.1 inputs at 48Gbps and good gaming features Decent sound quality Good build quality
*The not so good* HDR tone mapping is over-clipping detail higher than 600 nits Dynamic HDR tone mapping over brightening the image Some light DSE and banding seen Local dimming can be intrusive and quick scene changes catch it out
Join the discussion at AVForums - https://www.avforums.com/threads/hisense-u7k-65u7k-4k-mini-led-tv-review-comments.2466137/

item.title: Samsung QN95C 4K Mini LED TV Review - HUGE peak Brightness, BUT, is it any good?
item.description:
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/samsung-qn95c-qe65qn95c-4k-neo-qled-mini-led-tv-review.20938/
The Samsung QN95C is a step up from last year’s QN95B with slight improvements in picture quality and the ability to disable dynamic tone mapping for more accurate HDR images. Picture quality is very good and the HDR 10 performance offers exceptional brightness, colour reproduction and volume. Still, it is a shame there is no Dolby Vision support. This MiniLED 4K Flagship offers excellent bright room images but is held back by some aggressive blooming suppression that does limit the dynamic range of specular highlights to reduce clouding and haloing effects. Video processing is also good, if not quite as polished as the competition from Sony and LG. Gaming support offers up to four full-bandwidth HDMI 2.1 (48Gbps) ports with 4K/144Hz for PC gaming and 4K/120Hz console gaming, ALLM (Auto Low Latency Mode), eARC and FreeSync Premium Pro VRR (Variable Refresh Rate) as well as the Game Bar Menu and input lag that measures 9.3ms at 4K/60. Overall, the Samsung QN95C offers a polished performance with most sources for bright room viewing wrapped in a nice design with good build quality. It lacks the one-connect box and individual pixel response dynamic range capabilities of the S95C QD-OLED, but as a living room workhorse in bright conditions and with a mix of sources, it produces the goods. However, it is far too expensive for the technology and performance on offer.
*The good* Excellent peak brightness and full-screen brightness Is accurate with SDR and HDR content in Filmmaker Mode Four HDMI 2.1 inputs at 48Gbps Excellent gaming credentials Decent sound quality
*The not so good* No Dolby Vision support Aggressive blooming suppression reduces overall dynamic range capabilities Dynamic tone mapping can over-brighten the image, leave it set to Static Some light DSE and banding seen Some back-door processing is being applied
Join the discussion at AVForums - https://www.avforums.com/threads/samsung-qn95c-qe65qn95c-4k-mini-led-tv-review-discussion.2464423/
We use Portrait Displays’ Calman colour calibration software (https://www.portrait.com) a Murideo Seven Generator and a Klein K-10A meter profiled to a JETI Spectraval 1511-HiRes spectroradiometer for measurement and calibration.

item.title: BenQ W2710i (HT3560) 4K Projector Review - An Affordable 4K Home Theater Projector
item.description:
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/benq-w2710i-4k-dlp-projector-review.20783/
BenQ W2710i 4K DLP Projector Review - Also known as the HT3560 in the US.
Designed to be used in a dark room for critical movie viewing, the BenQ W2710i is a genuinely great DLP projector that produces accurate SDR images and has a decent stab at showing HDR content with an attempt to tone map to the capabilities of the projector.
Blacks are good and a darker shade of grey from traditional DLP home entertainment machines, with some decent shadow detail retrieval and only an odd instance of black crush seen within tricky mixed-light scenes. It’s not a push to describe the SDR image quality as cinematic and capable of excellent colour reproduction, with life-like skin tones and a natural-looking colour palette for this price point.
Motion and video processing are also very good for this level of the market with pulldown applied correctly to 24fps material. Overall, at the market position and price, the BenQ W2720i offers an excellent attempt at cinematic images for use in a dark room for critical viewing.
It doesn’t reach the cinematic highs of the latest laser-powered JVC and Sony units and you shouldn’t expect that from such a budget-conscious machine, but BenQ has done a great job with the W2710i. It’s a Best Buy.
*The Good* Excellent image accuracy in Filmmaker Mode out-of-the-box Superb calibrated performance ISF modes for locked settings following calibration Extensive calibration controls Very good video processing and motion Decent black levels that are dark grey and some decent shadow detail retrieval for a DLP projector Decent representation of HDR content which looks slightly brighter and more dynamic than SDR Good smart TV integration
*The Not So Good* Some black crush visible with tricky content scenes DCI-P3 tracking could be much better Noisy at 34db in HDR10 mode DLP lacks overall contrast for HDR

item.title: 🎬 Mission Impossible Dead Reckoning, Bruce Lee 4K, Evil Dead Rise 4K and The Bear Season 2 on TV
item.description:
This week we take a look at Tom Cruise’s latest must-see hit, the epic Mission: Impossible – Dead Reckoning Part 1, and wonder whether 2023 blockbuster entertainment could get any better than that; we cover Wes Anderson’s latest, Asteroid City, which is less engaging than the associated exhibition that’s running to celebrate the film in London, as well as Netflix’s Bird Box spin-off, and a number of juicy new 4K releases including Evil Dead: Rise and Arrow’s lavish Bruce Lee Box Set, as well as the original Avatar, and we also dig into some decent TV, including the Korean series Bloodhounds and the upcoming second seasons of The Bear and Asimov’s Foundation, which promise to be every bit as good as the first.
Presented by Cas Harlow with Mark Costello and Simon Crust

item.title: BenQ TK860i 4K Review - A Great Multi-Use Projector for Games, Sports and Movies
item.description:
Read the full in-depth review at AVForums - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/benq-tk860i-4k-dlp-projector-review.20784/
The BenQ TK860i is a hybrid projector for many use cases. While it never excels at any one thing in particular, the wide range of uses and good brightness will appeal to many users. It is not for critical movie viewing in a dark room, but for everything else, the TK860i offers good image quality for big-screen gaming, movies and sports in a normal living room environment with the lights off and curtains pulled.
*The Good* Good calibrated image accuracy Decent upscaling and video processing Good motion for 24fps and 50Hz broadcast Decent gaming performance 17.7ms input lag Good smart TV Good all-round performance for the money
*The Not So Good* Blacks are light grey rather than black Crushed blacks Not HDR capable but is compatible with HDR sources Lacks real contrast Not for critical movie viewing Noisy in HDR10 mode

item.title: Samsung S95C QD-OLED TV Review: 2nd Gen QD-OLED is STUNNING! COMPARED to S95B, QN95C and LG G3!
item.description:
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/samsung-s95c-qe55s95c-4k-qd-oled-tv-review.20917/
We thank UK retailer Peter Tyson for their assistance in providing a retail version of the 55-inch Samsung S95C for review and if you want to support our video reviews and channel and are looking for a new TV, then please visit their e-commerce website at https://www.petertyson.co.uk
The Samsung S95C is a step up from last year’s S95B with much better build quality and a gorgeous Infinity One design and One Connect box for source connections. Picture quality is also superb and HDR 10 performance offers some of the best high dynamic range images on the market with stunning colour reproduction and volume. Still, it is a shame there is no Dolby Vision support.
This 2nd generation QD-OLED review TV is a retail example and it manages to get close to what Samsung promised in terms of peak brightness and full-screen brightness while in an accurate picture mode. Video processing is also very good if not quite as polished as the competition from Sony and LG.
Gaming support is also excellent with four full-bandwidth HDMI 2.1 (48Gbps) ports and support for 4K at 144Hz (PC gaming) 4K/120Hz console gaming, ALLM (Auto Low Latency Mode), eARC and FreeSync Premium Pro VRR (Variable Refresh Rate) as well as the Game Bar Menu and input lag that measures 9.3ms at 4K/60.
Overall, the Samsung S95C is an excellent QD-OLED TV with all the benefits of that technology, wrapped in a much better design than last year and is certainly a *Best Buy*.
*The good* Stunning HDR images for colour volume Excellent peak brightness and full-screen brightness Very good black levels and shadow detail retrieval in dark room viewing Excels with high-quality 4K HDR sources Is very accurate with SDR and HDR content in Filmmaker Mode Four HDMI 2.1 inputs at 48Gbps Game Bar Decent sound quality Excellent build quality One Connect box Solar-powered remote Decent selection of in-built VOD apps Panel uniformity is very good
*The not so good* Blacks become dark grey and washed out in strong ambient lighting, the screen surface looks the same when switched off due to a lack of a filter No Dolby Vision support Dynamic tone mapping can over brighten the image quality, leave it set to Static Some back-door processing is being applied in SDR modes
Want the best picture settings to use with the Samsung S95C? Watch our video - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=umtgP59y5zI
In this video, we also compare the S95C with the LG G3, Samsung S95B and Samsung QN95C.
Read our review of the LG G3 - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/lg-g3-oled55g3-mla-oled-evo-tv-review.20853/ Watch our LG G3 review - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IQxmllotCQY
We use Portrait Displays’ Calman colour calibration software (https://www.portrait.com) a Murideo Seven Generator and a Klein K-10A meter profiled to a JETI Spectraval 1511-HiRes spectroradiometer for measurement and calibration.

item.title: Optoma UHZ50 DLP Projector Review - Can it do HDR?
item.description:
We take a look at the Optoma UHZ50 and you can read the in-depth review here - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/optoma-uhz50-4k-dlp-laser-projector-review.20723/
The Optoma UHZ50 offers a good entry point to laser-powered home entertainment DLP projection with a performance that gives you decent image quality for SDR movies, sports and gaming. It is a little weak when it comes to HDR, but no DLP projector at this price point will give you contrast, colour, or dynamic range that can create a convincing HDR image; however, there is a perceivable brightness difference compared to SDR content. This is not a projector for critical home cinema movie viewing as blacks are grey and there is a lack of contrast and crushed blacks, but it doesn’t pretend to be anything other than a fun, useful all-rounder for casual gaming, sports and movies. Overall, with excellent input lag for gaming, and a decently bright image for most white-coloured rooms, thanks to the use of a laser light source and the portability of a projector, this perfectly fits the home entertainment branding and provides a good all-round performance.
*The good* Laser light source for instant on/off and lifespan Good value for money as an all-round big screen projector Colour and greyscale are good with SDR content out of the box Can be used with a wide variety of content types Looks bright, sharp and vivid in the right conditions Good input lag for SDR gaming on a big screen The potential of PC gaming at 1080/240hz ISF modes 3D, if that’s still your thing…
*The not so good* Lacks real contrast Weak black levels and crushed blacks Not an HDR projector or for critical movie viewing Video processing has slight issues with upscaling, motion and colour gradations Streaming quality and app support is poor Speakers sound thin and should only be used in emergencies Pricey when compared to the recent competition

item.title: The BEST TV of 2023? LG G3 MLA OLED Evo TV Review - COMPARED to Samsung S95C & QN95C
item.description:
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/lg-g3-oled55g3-mla-oled-evo-tv-review.20853/
We thank UK retailer Peter Tyson for their assistance in providing a retail version of the 55-inch LG G3 for review and if you want to support our video reviews and channel and are looking for a new TV, then please visit their e-commerce website at https://www.petertyson.co.uk
Peter Tyson is offering AVForums viewers an *exclusive £100 OFF the LG OLED55G36LA* until the end of June 2023. Just use the voucher code *AVF100* at checkout. https://petertyson.co.uk/lg-oled55g36la-55-uhd-smart-television-soloco
The G3 is the flagship 4K model from LG for 2023 and it features for the first time Micro Lens Array MLA technology which is a layer of billions of micrometre-sized convex lenses fixed to the pixels that capture and direct light usually lost within a traditional OLED panel and redirects this towards the viewer.
By redirecting this light towards the viewer, LG has boosted brightness and viewing angle stability enormously. This is married to the Brightness Booster Pro processing that uses a brightness-enhancing algorithm, which improves screen brightness and colour by analysing and adjusting the brightness of each scene in real-time and adding more specular details and much better just above-black detail to enhance HDR performance.
In this video, we give you our review of the LG G3 OLED TV as well as comparisons against the Samsung S95C QD-OLED and the QN95C MiniLED TVs.
We use Portrait Displays’ Calman colour calibration software (https://www.portrait.com) a Murideo Seven Generator and a Klein K-10A meter profiled to a JETI Spectraval 1511-HiRes spectroradiometer for measurement and calibration.

Peter Tyson is offering AVForums viewers an *exclusive £100 OFF the LG OLED55G36LA* until the end of June 2023. Just use the voucher code *AVF100* at checkout. https://petertyson.co.uk/lg-oled55g36la-55-uhd-smart-television-soloco
The G3 is the flagship 4K model from LG for 2023 and it features for the first time Micro Lens Array MLA technology which is a layer of billions of micrometre-sized convex lenses fixed to the pixels that capture and direct light usually lost within a traditional OLED panel and redirects this towards the viewer.
By redirecting this light towards the viewer, LG has boosted brightness and viewing angle stability enormously. This is married to the Brightness Booster Pro processing that uses a brightness-enhancing algorithm, which improves screen brightness and colour by analysing and adjusting the brightness of each scene in real-time and adding more specular details and much better just above-black detail to enhance HDR performance.
In this video, we give you our review of the LG G3 OLED TV as well as comparisons against the Samsung S95C QD-OLED and the QN95C MiniLED TVs.
We use Portrait Displays’ Calman colour calibration software (https://www.portrait.com) a Murideo Seven Generator and a Klein K-10A meter profiled to a JETI Spectraval 1511-HiRes spectroradiometer for measurement and calibration.

item.title: LG G3 MLA OLED Evo Best Picture Settings - works for ALL 2023 LG OLEDs
item.description:
We go through the best out-of-the-box picture settings for SDR, HDR and Dolby Vision on the brand-new LG G3 Micro Lens Array (MLA) OLED Evo TV. These settings make sure that you see TV, Sports and Film content as it was mastered and intended to be seen, without a full professional calibration. We measured these settings to make sure they are accurate to the standards and you can see those within the reviews at AVForums. These settings also work with any LG OLED sets with Filmmaker Mode.
Peter Tyson are offering AVForums readers an exclusive £100 OFF the LG OLED55G36LA until the end of June 2023. Just use the voucher code AVF100 at checkout. https://petertyson.co.uk/lg-oled55g36la-55-uhd-smart-television-soloco
The 55-inch LG G3 was supplied to us on long-term loan by UK retailer Peter Tyson and is a retail unit and not a manufacturer-supplied TV. Support like this means that we can produce long-term reviews and comparisons of the latest flagship TVs meaning you get unbiased and accurate information based on actual retail TVs you can buy. If you are looking for a TV and want to support our channel then please consider using Peter Tyson for a great deal and tell them we sent you! Visit - https://www.petertyson.co.uk/
Read the full in-depth review of the LG G3 - coming soon
The LG G3 OLED Evo TV is the flagship model in the 4K TV line-up from the South Korean brand for 2023 and brings to the market Micro Lens Array (MLA) for the first time on an LG TV, which significantly boosts image brightness and dynamic range. LG Display describes this as 3rd Generation META Premium OLED technology and LG Electronics will not even use the terminology MLA, instead, they call it Light Control Architecture with Brightness Booster Max technology. But whatever the politics or nomenclature are, the benefit is clear to see within the first few minutes of watching the LG G3.
We only ever supply tested and measured settings free of charge and based on getting close to the industry standards so you can watch TV and film content as it was mastered and intended to be seen.

item.title: Sony A84L/A80L BRAVIA XR OLED TV Review - COMPARED to LG C3, Samsung QD-OLED & LG G3
item.description:
*Read the full in-depth review* - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/sony-a84l-a80l-xr-65a84l-bravia-xr-oled-tv-review.20826/ The Sony A84L/A80L is a solid OLED TV that offers excellent image quality, a unique 3.2 Acoustic Surface Audio+ technology where the screen becomes the speaker, two HDMI 2.1 inputs with support for 4K/120, VRR, and ALLM, along with a decent input lag of 16.3ms.
It uses an LGD-supplied WRGB OLED panel and not a QD-OLED model, plus, it doesn’t feature a heatsink for extra brightness or MLA technology, but that doesn’t mean it can’t produce excellent calibrated images, inky blacks and decent dynamic range.
It is an impressive mid-range model that offers superb video processing, accurate calibrated images, natural-looking skin tones and colours, along with very good motion. There are a few small issues for the A84L which revolve around the slightly better-specified and cheaper competition from the likes of LG C3 which offers very similar performance and better out-of-the-box accuracy, but the Sony A84L/A80L offers enough to warrant a recommendation.
*The good* Decent calibrated SDR performance and accuracy Very good HDR10 and Dolby Vision performance Cognitive Processor XR image quality Excellent video upscaling and processing Very good motion with film and 50Hz TV show content Auto Calibration with Calman AutoCal Great sound quality from Acoustic Surface Audio+ for everyday TV viewing Google TV is stable and fast TV stand options Great build quality
*The not so good* Custom Mode is not accurate out of the box (No Filmmaker Mode) Lacks brightness in HDR compared to rivals Cyan tint to images in Custom Mode Only two HDMI 2.1 (48Gbps) inputs
We use Portrait Displays’ Calman colour calibration software (https://www.portrait.com) a Murideo Seven Generator and a Klein K-10A meter profiled to a JETI Spectraval 1511-HiRes spectroradiometer for measurement and calibration.

item.title: ⭐ WORTH IT? LG C3 OLED Evo Review - COMPARED to LG C2, Samsung QD OLED & Sony A84L
item.description:
*Read the full in-depth review* - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/lg-c3-oled65c3-oled-evo-tv-review.20771/
Once again the C series model in the LG OLED line-up offers excellent all-round performance with a good mix of features, picture quality and gaming credentials. The C3 continues what has gone before and the upgrade from the 2022 C2 model is not huge, but then why fix something that wasn’t really broken? There is slightly more brightness on offer thanks to the Alpha 9 AI Processor 4K Gen6 chip and the latest OLED panel, which when combined together are classed as OLED Evo, plus, like last year, the video processing is now some of the best on the market for upscaling, detail, smooth gradation and motion. But, if you don’t need the slight increase in brightness, the slightly better processing or the newly designed WebOS and quick menu, you could pick up the 2022 65-inch C2 which is almost identical performance-wise for close to £1200 less (in May 2023). We have no doubt that the C3 pricing will also follow the same course over a year that the C2 has, so the choice, as they say, is yours.
*The good* 👍 Excellent accuracy out of the box in Filmmaker Mode 👍 Superb 3D LUT calibration capabilities & AutoCal 👍 Superb video processing from the a9 Gen6 AI processor 👍 Very good just above black performance in SDR and HDR 👍 Excellent 24fps & 50Hz motion 👍 Upscaling is superb 👍 Superb HDR accuracy 👍 Dolby Vision / HDR10 / HLG / DV IQ 👍 Improved panel uniformity 👍 Dolby Atmos & DTS support 👍 Superb gaming features and four HDMI 2.1 (48Gbps) ports 👍 WebOS 23 👍 Excellent design and materials 👍 WOW Orchestra integration with optional USC9S soundbar and subwoofer
*The not so good* 👎 No HDR10+/HDR10+ Adaptive 👎 WebOS 23 top third advertising space is not welcome and is a waste of screen real estate 👎 No backlight on the remote 👎 Sound quality is only serviceable via built-in speakers 👎 Expensive at the time of launch (£200 more expensive vs. C2 launch)
Watch our *Best Settings* Video for the LG C3 here - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=--f8PLK3MKU
We use Portrait Displays’ Calman colour calibration software (https://www.portrait.com) a Murideo Seven Generator and a Klein K-10A meter profiled to a JETI Spectraval 1511-HiRes spectroradiometer for measurement and calibration.

item.title: 🎬 Guardians Vol 3, Michael J Fox’s Still, Air, Musketeers 4K, Fear & Loathing 4K, Daisy & Beef on TV
item.description:
This week Tom talks about the latest, good, Marvel movie, Guardians of the Galaxy Volume 3, and Apple’s release of Michael J. Fox's Still. Mark has a meeting about Amazon's "Meetings: The Movie", Air, and both classic Musketeers movies in 4K, 1973's The Three Musketeers and 1974's The Four Musketeers. And Simon assesses Fear and Loathing in 4K and talks up Apple’s Silo and Netflix's Beef on TV, plus may give us a Brotherhood of the Wolf 4K unboxing!
Presented by Tom Davies with Mark Costello and Simon Crust

item.title: LG C3 OLED Evo BEST Picture SETTINGS | 2023 All Screen Sizes
item.description:
Read our full review of the LG C3 OLED Evo TV here - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/lg-c3-oled65c3-oled-evo-tv-review.20771/ These settings can be used with all 2023 LG TVs. These are the best out-of-the-box settings to get the image quality as close as possible to the industry standards so you can view film and TV content as it was mastered and intended to be seen. These are not calibrated settings as it is not advised to share calibrated settings as they should be for your individual video chain, room and environment and performed using a meter, pattern generator and software as the eye is incapable of making such adjustments.
We only ever supply tested and measured settings free of charge and based on getting close to the industry standards so you can watch TV and film content as it was mastered and intended to be seen.

item.title: 🎬 Super Mario, Renfield, 4K reviews of Plane, Picnic at Hanging Rock and Naked Lunch, and True Lies
item.description:
This week we talk about how Nicolas Cage might be the best thing at the cinemas at the moment - Renfield going up against the likes of Super Mario Bros., Assassin Club and Mummies - discuss the best and worst Superman sequel from the original series, investigate some good Gerard Butler on 4K in the form of Plane, Second Sight’s latest lavish box set in Picnic at Hanging Rock 4K, Arrow’s latest - Cronenberg’s Naked Lunch in 4K - and Arrow’s upcoming release of the next highly anticipated Michael Mann release… Blackhat. Plus we catch up on Mando, Picard and some of the best other TV out there like The Last Thing He Told Me, The Night Agent, Slasher and Shrinking… but NOT True Lies.
Presented by Cas Harlow with Mark Costello, Simon Crust and Tom Davies

item.title: 🛠️ Sharp FN2 Plus every 2021-2023 Sharp TV | Best Picture Settings Out Of The Box
item.description:
For free, here are our suggested settings for the Sharp FN2 and every 2021, 2022 and 2023 Sharp TV available in the UK, with the same OS as the set in this video. We choose the Movie preset for SDR, Movie (HDR) preset for HDR and Dolby Vision Dark for DV content. We don't change any other settings as the defaults in these modes get the TV very close to the industry standards out of the box to view content as it was mastered and intended to be seen. These are not calibrated settings, they are the best out-of-the-box settings.

item.title: ⭐ Sharp 55FN2KA LED LCD TV Review | A GOOD 2nd Room TV Choice?
item.description:
The Sharp 55FN2KA is an entry-level LED LCD Android TV which offers decent picture quality and features for the price point. It is not designed for critical movie watching and doesn’t stand up well in dark room viewing, but used as intended in a well-lit living room or second room and the Sharp offers decent value for money with accurate colours and greyscale, mixed with a good amount of streaming apps and features. It also sounds good considering the price point and should be considered if you’re looking for a budget second screen TV for non-critical viewing.
⭐ Read the full in-depth review with measurements and calibration results - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/sharp-55fn2ka-led-lcd-tv-review-dolby-vision-hdr10-android-game-mode-harman-kardon.20653/
We use Portrait Displays’ Calman colour calibration software (https://www.portrait.com) a Murideo Seven Generator and a Klein K-10A meter profiled to a JETI Spectraval 1511-HiRes spectroradiometer for measurement and calibration.

item.title: 🎬 Rocky 4K, Creed 3 and boxing movies, Shazam 2, 65 vs Jurassic World Dominion, + Picard & Mando
item.description:
We're back and going boxing for the first part of the podcast, talking about the Rocky films cleaning up in 4K, and Creed 3 reigning at the box office, and really looking at boxing movies and what makes them work. There's more DC at the cinema too with Shazam 2, whilst we STILL wait for The Flash which is still being touted as the greatest superhero movie ever made ever. And dinosaurs are back, with 65 proving a whole lot more fun than anything else Jurassic in years. And we look at some quality sci-fi/fantasy TV, discussing if they figured out how to course-correct on Picard, or are likely to fall at the last hurdle? And Mando’s back - does it make up for The Fett?
Presented by Cas Harlow with Simon Crust and Mark Costello
This weeks podcast is sponsored by by MPB, the largest global platform to buy, sell and trade used photo and video kit, visit us at www.mpb.com

item.title: 🎤 Exclusive Interview with Disc Producer Jasper Sharp from Arrow Video
item.description:
This week we have an exclusive interview with Producer Jasper Sharp, from Arrow Video, taking a look at his background in writing, directing and now producing titles, some of the discs he has worked on, including Arrow's Battle Royale 4K and Ju-On The Grudge 4K sets, and his latest release, The House that Screamed, what it takes to get a disc out, sourcing the cuts and extra material, and what he thinks of the future of physical media.
Presented by Cas Harlow with Mark Costello

item.title: 🎤 Sony A95L QD-OLED, X95L MINI LED And Full BRAVIA Range For 2023 (In-Depth Interview).
item.description:
Sony held their European TV launch in Weybridge on the 22nd of February and I was invited along to check out the new models in person and get hands-on. You can watch the in-depth video with an interview with Gavin McCarron from Sony. The big news is the flagship TV will be the A95L QD-OLED with a new 77-inch screen size available. There is also a new stand design so it doesn’t have the lean-back monolith design of the A95K and is better suited for use with a centre speaker or soundbar if required. It also features the new QD-OLED panel from Samsung Display for 2023 with a high-brightness blue EL giving a big jump in overall brightness, especially for full-field white and specular highlights. Added to that is the increased colour volume compared to WOLED and some new processing features from the BRAVIA XR processor including XR Clear Image. There is also Acoustic Surface Audio+ which uses the screen to create the sound and this also features Acoustic Centre Sync, 3D Surround Upscaling, 360 Spatial Sound Personaliser and Ambient optimisation along with support for Dolby Vision 120HZ gaming and two HDMI 2.1 (48Gbps) inputs with VRR, ALLM and eARC thanks to the Pentonic 1000 chip being used. Other game features include a new game menu, dual view and the ability to reduce the picture size to best suit your games and immersive experience. BRAVIA Core is also included with 10 credits and 24 months of free streaming along with BRAVIA CAM being included and the Smart OS is Google TV. The samples of the A95L seen at the event were very early pre-production units so I am unable to give you any details on the image quality and I’ll have to wait until finished retail samples are available for review, but it looks like a promising upgrade over last year’s model.
The step-down WOLED model for 2023 is the A80L OLED available in screen sizes of 55-, 65-, 77- and 83-inches with pricing yet to be determined. Features include the BRAVIA XR processor with the new XR Clear Image feature, Acoustic Surface Audio+ with the same audio features as the A95L, you get the same 10 credits and free 24 months of BRAVIA CORE streaming, Google TV and support for Dolby Vision, HDR10 and HLG HDR formats and a new positional stand design. There is also the black hairline simple remote control. So in terms of OLED TVs, Sony feels they offer something for everyone.
Read more... - https://www.avforums.com/news/sony-a95l-qd-oled-x95l-mini-led-and-full-bravia-tv-line-up-announced.20613/

item.title: 🎬 Ant-Man’s Quantumania, Wakanda 4K + Eight for Silver, Alice Darling, Empire of Light & Picard
item.description:
We’re going small for this podcast and talking about the latest Marvel entry at the cinema, Ant-Man and The Wasp: Quantumania, the latest Marvel movie on 4K, Black Panther: Wakanda Forever, and the question that keeps popping up for most MCU fans - will it ever get back on track after Endgame? I guess with Feige’s new 80-year plan he’s leaving the answer to that question in the hands of his successor(s).
So Mark’s going to tell us about what everybody should really be watching right now - Eight for Silver - as well as talking about The Woman King on 4K and why Picard may be good again, Tom will be reviewing Ant-Man and singing the praises of Lockwood on Netflix, whilst Simon’s still training for his Rocky 4K collection review. And, apart from Wakanda 4K, I’ll be talking about Alice, Darling and Empire of Light, and the final season of Carnival Row.
Presented by Cas Harlow with Tom Davies, Simon Crust and Mark Costello
This weeks podcast is sponsored by by MPB, the largest global platform to buy, sell and trade used photo and video kit, visit us at www.mpb.com

item.title: Philips Reveals New OLED TVs, ISE 2023 Report, Paradigm Multichannel Speaker Review + AV/HiFi News
item.description:
This week; Phil looks at the latest Ambilight TVs revealed at the recent Philips event in Amsterdam and Jules fills us in on the ISE exhibition in Barcelona. There’re also reviews of the SVS Prime Wireless Pro speakers and the NAD C 3050LE integrated amp.
Plus, after the TV community’s hopes were raised with talk of support for 4x fully featured HDMI 2.1 ports, we talk about the disappointing news that the MediaTek Pentonic 1000 chip will still only cater for two, and what it means for TV manufacturers. There’s also our usual AV and Hi-Fi news roundup.
Presented by Phil Hinton with Ed Selley, Ian Collen, Martin Dew and Julian Scott.
This week's podcast is sponsored by MPB, the largest global platform to buy, sell and trade used photo and video kit, visit us at www.mpb.com

item.title: Is 8K TV dead? Philips OLED+907, Pioneer LX505 AVR plus B&W 700 S3 Reviews & Visit + AV/HiFi News
item.description:
This week; Phil talks about his recent trip to Bowers & Wilkins while Ed takes a look at the company’s 705 S3 speaker. There’re also reviews of the Philips OLED+907 TV, Pioneer’s VSX-LX505 AVR and a power amp from Parasound.
Plus, after our recent trip to Las Vegas, we ask if the lack of consumer 8K TVs at CES 2023 indicates that the technology has failed to take off and what it means for TV manufacturers. There’s also our usual AV and Hi-Fi news roundup.
Presented by Phil Hinton with Ed Selley, Ian Collen and Doug Pyper
This week’s podcast is sponsored by the new Bowers & Wilkins 700 Series https://www.bowerswilkins.com/en-gb/speakers/loudspeakers/700-series?clickId=4267748223

item.title: CES 2023 Round Up: New TV Lineups for 2023 from LG, Samsung, Panasonic, Hisense & TCL
item.description:
Back from Las Vegas, we kick off the year with a CES 2023 podcast special. There’s plenty to look forward to with new QD-OLED TVs from Samsung, brighter MLA OLEDs from LG and Panasonic, and mini LED models across the board.
There was also a chance to find out about developments from Dirac and MediaTek which promise new, exciting features for AV enthusiasts.
Presented by Phil Hinton with; Ian Collen, Julian Scott and Martin Dew

item.title: Bowers & Wilkins Diamond Surround System in the BMW iX M60: Is this the best car audio system ever?
item.description:
In a special New Year's video, we look at the new BMW iX M60 EV and the Diamond Surround System fitted to it from Bowers & Wilkins. Just how does this £117K EV stand up when tested first as a modern Electric Vehicle then we set about reviewing the B&W audio system. With no engine sound to get in the way and an ultra-rigid chassis, is this the best car Hi-Fi system produced so far? Let's find out...

item.title: Home cinema, Hi-Fi and AV highlights of 2022 plus favourite movies, 4K discs, TV shows and games
item.description:
Our final podcast of the year is a Christmas special which sees the Hardware and Movies teams get together for a festive round table look back at the highlights of 2022 as they discuss the products, technologies, innovations and content that made the year stand out… or not!
And our valued patrons get to hang around after the episode too and ask questions and chat with the panel as a Xmas thank you.
Presented by Phil Hinton with Ed Selley, Ian Collen, Julian Scott, Martin Dew, Cas Harlow and Mark Costello.

item.title: Philips OLED+907 & OLED+937, plus, a Philips QD OLED in 2023? - In conversation with Danny Tack
item.description:
We visit the Philips office in Gent, Belgium to speak at length with Danny Tack, Senior Director of Product Strategy & Planning about the new OLED+907 and OLED+937 TVs as well finding out how Philips plan for new technologies, test and benchmark their products and what they have planned for the future. Danny also discloses that they are testing QD OLED and have some in-house prototypes for assessment. Will they launch a QD-OLED in 2023?
The interview took place in Gent in late September 2022. The 'Includes paid promotion' marker is included due to Philips sponsoring this video. Discover more at https://www.philips.com/oled

item.title: 🎬 Fidelity in Motion's David Mackenzie talks about his work on disc encoding & the future of Blu-ray
item.description:
This week Cas and the team have a special guest star - Fidelity in Motion’s David Mackenzie, a former AVForums reviewer who talks about starting up his own encoding company, what makes a good encode, some of the best projects he’s worked on, tackling director’s intent with the technology on hand in the modern age, SDR vs HDR10 vs Dolby Vision, and the future of physical media.
Presented by Cas Harlow with Simon Crust and Mark Costello
00:00:00 - Start 00:00:28 - Welcome 00:02:07 - About David Mackenzie 00:12:41 - David M Blu-ray encoding reputation 00:17:57 - Is Blu-ray encoding adjusted on a scene by scene basis? 00:19:32 - How is a movie encoded on to a Blu-ray disc? 00:31:54 - Is fluctuating bitrate bad? 00:33:35 - Is encoding different on Blu-ray vs streaming? 00:39:35 - What's the biggest challenge when encoding a Blu-ray? 00:41:27 - Are there tell-tale signs of a bad encode? 00:44:15 - What are David's favourite encodes? 00:46:39 - DNR (dynamic noise reduction) or no DNR? 00:56:34 - HDR (high dynamic range) vs SDR (standard dynamic range) 01:03:40 - Is 4K Blu-ray the last optical disc format? 01:10:23 - Why haven't some big movies come to 4K Blu-ray yet? 01:12:06 - Mulholland Drive encoding story segway 01:21:39 - Is there often print damage? 01:25:25 - About seamless branching encoding

item.title: JVC 4K projectors, Denon X3800 & Perlisten speaker reviews, adding a sub to 2-channel + AV/HiFi news
item.description:
This week, Phil reviews the JVC NZ7 and NP5 4K projectors, revealing the differences between laser and bulb based light sources. Doug goes ‘high end’ with the Peristen Audio S-Series 5.1 speaker system and ‘affordable’ with the Denon AVC-X3800H AV receiver. Meanwhile, Ed checks out the PSB Passif 50 speakers and explains what to consider when adding a subwoofer to a 2-channel music set up.
Also, Jules will take us behind the scenes into the world of display calibration training and there’s the usual look at the latest AV and Hi-Fi news.
Presented by Phil Hinton with Ed Selley, Ian Collen, Julian Scott and Doug Pyper

item.title: What is the best TV in 2022 for watching movies and TV drama series?
item.description:
If you’re a movie fan and want to see films and TV dramas as they were mastered and intended to be seen, there is currently no finer TV on the market than the Sony A95K QD-OLED. It really is a master class in picture quality with stunning colour reproduction, spotless uniformity, stunning upscaling and picture processing capabilities, with those amazing blacks and sublime dynamic range. Bravo to the BRAVIA! It’s a Best in Class award winner for the ultimate in movie watching excellence.
It therefore also wins the Editor's Choice award for Best TV 2022, Read the full review here: https://www.avforums.com/reviews/sony-a95k-bravia-xr-55a95k-qd-oled-tv-review.20028/ What the full video review here: https://www.avforums.com/reviews/video-review-sony-bravia-xr-a95k-qd-oled-review.20074/ Watch our Editor's Choice award video here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hAngWcySdUc

item.title: JVC NZ7 projector & Arcam AVR21 reviews, Pro vs. home calibration, the new Sky Stream + AV/HiFi news
item.description:
On the podcast this week, we ask if the new Sky Stream device is the answer for TV fans who want to keep Sky content on their own TV but drop the satellite dish - Phil gives us a preview. He also reviews the JVC NZ7 4K laser projector and introduces Doug, the newest member of the review team who gives us the lowdown on the Arcam AVR21 AV receiver.
Resident display calibration guru Dr. Jules runs through the main differences between calibrating for professional clients versus what home users require, while over in the world of Hi-Fi, Ed reviews the Cyrus Classic Amp and presents his music recommendations for the episode. Plus there’s the latest AV, home cinema and Hi-Fi related news, live questions from our viewers, and much more.
Presented by Phil Hinton with Ed Selley, Ian Collen, Julian Scott and Doug Pyper.

item.description:

item.title: Philips OLED+937 & OLED+907 TVs launch with Heat Sink, OLED EX Panels and Bowers & Wilkins Sound
item.description:
Philips announced two new OLED+ models in Berlin recently and we attended the launch event. Read the article - https://www.avforums.com/news/philips-showcases-new-ambilight-oled-and-mini-led-tvs.20088/
The headline act is the OLED+937, available in 65- and 77-inch variants. With the enhanced processing chip and OLED EX panel equipped with heat sync, the model can boast a peak brightness of 1300 nits. It also offers Advanced HDR across “all the main HDR formats” to optimise its effect by tone mapping the content on a frame-by-frame basis, rather than just from one scene to the next. As part of the new generation of Ambilight technology, the OLED+937 is also one of the first in the range to enable individual control over each rear-mounted LED to further increase the range and precision of colours on the screen.
As part of Philips’ ongoing partnership with Bowers & Wilkins, the OLED+937 also comes with an impressive sound system that now comes with dedicated left and right side-firing speakers for the first time in a 5.1.2 set-up with a combined 95W output. Gamers will appreciate the G-Sync and FreeSync Premium support, along with the new VRR Shadow Enhancer that aims to improve performance against those all-important variable refresh rates.
The OLED+907 is only slightly smaller in stature, offering up 48-, 55-, and 65-inch screens and featuring the same upgraded processing power of the 937. It also has the same peak output of 1300 nits on the two larger displays and what seems to be much the same gamer-friendly support with variable refresh rates up to 4K in its monitor mode. The 907 has a slightly slimmed-down 3.1-channel, 80W Bowers & Wilkins sound system, with six front-mounted drivers in a more traditional LCR set-up, along with its rear-mounted sub backed up by four passive radiators.

It also offers Advanced HDR across “all the main HDR formats” to optimise its effect by tone mapping the content on a frame-by-frame basis, rather than just from one scene to the next. As part of the new generation of Ambilight technology, the OLED+937 is also one of the first in the range to enable individual control over each rear-mounted LED to further increase the range and precision of colours on the screen.
As part of Philips’ ongoing partnership with Bowers & Wilkins, the OLED+937 also comes with an impressive sound system that now comes with dedicated left and right side-firing speakers for the first time in a 5.1.2 set-up with a combined 95W output. Gamers will appreciate the G-Sync and FreeSync Premium support, along with the new VRR Shadow Enhancer that aims to improve performance against those all-important variable refresh rates.
The OLED+907 is only slightly smaller in stature, offering up 48-, 55-, and 65-inch screens and featuring the same upgraded processing power of the 937. It also has the same peak output of 1300 nits on the two larger displays and what seems to be much the same gamer-friendly support with variable refresh rates up to 4K in its monitor mode. The 907 has a slightly slimmed-down 3.1-channel, 80W Bowers & Wilkins sound system, with six front-mounted drivers in a more traditional LCR set-up, along with its rear-mounted sub backed up by four passive radiators.

item.title: ⭐ Sony A95K QD OLED Review: The Best TV of 2022? 10/10?
item.description:
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/sony-a95k-bravia-xr-55a95k-qd-oled-tv-review.20028/
There is no such thing as the perfect TV and this is important to remember as we continue to assess the best 2022 has to offer us. There are things this Sony A95K does that are sublime as well as ridiculous. The design will split opinions, it can’t easily be used with a soundbar and there are only two HDMI 2.1 inputs, which means it struggles with next-generation gaming PCs and console support, and one of those ports also has to be used as the eARC port if you have a device which requires that compatibility, cutting your available HDMI 2.1 ports to one. But, not all of those negatives will be negatives for everyone. We all have our own needs when it comes to a TV. If any of the above negatives are an issue for you, then the Sony A95K QD OLED is probably not for you, and that’s before we come on to the high price point.
But, if you’re a movie fan and want to see films and TV dramas as they were mastered and intended to be seen, there is currently no finer TV on the market than the Sony A95K QD-OLED. It really is a master class in picture quality with stunning colour reproduction, spotless uniformity, stunning upscaling and picture processing capabilities, with those amazing blacks and sublime dynamic range. Bravo to the BRAVIA! It’s a Best in Class award winner for the ultimate in movie watching excellence.
Join the discussion - https://www.avforums.com/threads/sony-a95k-bravia-xr-55a95k-qd-oled-tv-review-comments.2423892/

item.title: ⭐ Samsung QN95B 4K QLED TV Review
item.description:
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/samsung-qn95b-qe65qn95b-4k-neo-qled-tv-review.19992/ This is Samsung’s top-of-the-range 4K Neo QLED TV for 2022 and as such it is packed with the latest features from the company. It is a direct replacement for the outgoing QN95A from last year and in almost all respects, it is essentially the same TV, but with some minor tweaks to the Mini LED backlight and processing. As an all-round living room flagship, it certainly offers plenty of strong points from image brightness and colour accuracy, to strong blacks and decent HDR10 performance. Motion is also good and the video processing manages to provide decent upscaled images. However, the problem for the QN95B is the new stablemate QD-OLED S95B which offers all of these positives, but with per-pixel black levels and even better colour purity due to perfect blacks. Plus, due to the local dimming trying to suppress blooming artefacts from small bright areas of the image close to black backgrounds, by lowering the overall picture brightness, the usual brightness advantage of QLED isn’t as pronounced as it once was, but, it still has the size advantage of 75-and 85-inch models. The QN95B is a strong QLED model that will offer many plus points for many end users, but it does lose a point on the QN95A as it doesn’t quite move the QLED game on in any groundbreaking way, and the competition, even from within, is much more intense in 2022. We also find the pricing of £3,399.00 at the time of this review to be far too expensive given the competition. It is not value for money in my opinion.
Join the discussion at https://www.avforums.com/threads/samsung-qn95b-qe65qn95b-4k-neo-qled-tv-review-comments.2421529/

item.title: ⭐ Samsung QN800B 8K QLED TV Review
item.description:
Read the full in-depth review here - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/samsung-qn800b-qe65qn800b-8k-neo-qled-tv-review.19998/ The Samsung 65-inch QN800B is a good quality 8K Neo QLED TV with generally good picture quality for SDR and HDR content, with plenty of useful features and a very good OS and Smart TV system. It sounds decent thanks to OTS+, has a well-designed look and comes with the slim-line One Connect box, which makes it ideal for wall mounting. Whether 8K is a good choice for a TV in today’s market is really only a question you can answer and in our side-by-side testing, we were pushed to see any real difference between 4K and 8K in resolution terms from our normal seating distance. There is also a lack of Dolby Vision support, as there is with all Samsung TVs and it is very expensive at £3,499 at the time of this review in 2022. The QN800B is also up against some serious OLED competition this year, including Samsung’s own S95B QD-OLED and with such a crowded market, it may struggle to find an audience.
Join the conversation at AVForums - https://www.avforums.com/threads/samsung-qn800b-qe65qn800b-8k-neo-qled-tv-review-comments.2421993/

item.title: ⭐ Samsung S95B QD-OLED Review - A Quantum Leap for OLED!
item.description:
The Samsung S95B is a very promising start to the QD-OLED revolution with this first generation set offering excellent blacks, good shadow detail and stunning colour volume and brightness. Recent firmware updates have seen improvements in the out-of-the-box Filmmaker Mode accuracy and a PQ EOTF that now tracks the ST2084 standard correctly without over brightening HDR content. As a result, the S95B produces some of the best HDR10 content we have seen from an OLED TV with stunning detail, brightness and colour. In the most accurate Filmmaker Mode, the S95B is capable of some of the best colour volume we have yet seen from an OLED, that does make itself known within actual viewing content, and not just with test patterns. It’s not all perfect, but then there is no such thing as the perfect TV, however, the Samsung S95B is a stunning QD-OLED TV and easily picks up a Best Buy badge
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/samsung-s95b-qd-oled-tv-review.19923/
Join the conversation at AVForums - https://www.avforums.com/threads/samsung-s95b-qd-oled-tv-review-comments.2418140/
The Samsung S95B featured in this review video was purchased by AVForums from a UK retailer for long-term review.
We use (www.portrait.com) Portrait Displays' Calman color calibration software, a Murideo Seven Generator and a Klein K-10A meter for measurement and calibration.

item.title: ⭐ Philips OLED+986 TV Review
item.description:
In this video, we review the Philips OLED+986 TV. You can read our full in-depth review at AVForums - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/philips-65oled-plus-986-tv-review.19663/
The Philips OLED+986 is a niche within a niche. It’s an audiophile aimed TV with a Bowers and Wilkins speaker bar that promises high-end sound with high-quality images. It’s all wrapped up in a love it or hate it design with excellent build quality along with high-end aspirations. But does that suit the typical AVForums reader and member? Only you can truly answer that question, but as a film, console gaming, sport and TV program watching display, it works well with excellent OLED image quality and a superb two-channel Bowers & Wilkins sound. If you’re looking for Dolby Atmos overhead effects and film bass though, the OLED+936 is the TV you need to seek out as it offers up-firing speakers and a sub output. Moreover, the design of the OLED+986 also restricts its appeal to end-users and while gaming is good, it's not future-proofed with no ability to offer full resolution 4K/120 VRR support now or in the future... However, if the OLED+986 fits your requirements and needs, it’s certainly worthy of your demo time and comes recommended.
Visit the Philips TV Forum at AVForums - https://www.avforums.com/forums/philips-tvs-forum.114/
We use (www.portrait.com) Portrait Displays' Calman color calibration software, a Murideo Seven Generator and a Klein K-10A meter for measurement and calibration.

item.title: ⭐ Sky Glass Review | There is nothing magic about this TV
item.description:
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/sky-glass-tv-65-inch-review.19432/ On paper, Sky Glass TV promises an impressive package of convergence between the traditional TV, apps, no dish Sky TV, good sound and unique subscription-based pricing where in theory, you only need one (power) cable running to the set. The reality is altogether different with a promising if highly frustrating UI, married to a budget level TV with mediocre picture quality, that lacks dynamic range robbing HDR content of its highlights and ultimate pop. This first-generation version of Glass showed promise but it requires some serious reworking for those of us who want decent picture quality to match the connected ambitions of Sky. As it stands, the separate route of a decent Smart TV, solid soundbar with subwoofer and a Sky Q box (if you must have Sky), is still your best option to achieve the goals set out here in the best possible quality.
We use (www.portrait.com) Portrait Displays' Calman color calibration software, a Murideo Seven Generator and Klein K-10A meter for measurement and calibration.

item.title: A look at Sony's A95K QD OLED, A90K & A80K OLEDs and X95K mini LED TV | AVForums Podcast 24 Feb '22
item.description:
Sony's A95K is the first TV to be released using the Quantum Dot OLED display from Samsung Display. Our first up-close look at the TV reveals a return to the Monolith design, an updated Audio Surface Pro and definite image differences when compared directly with last year's A90J OLED. Our recent visit to Sony UK also gave us the opportunity to see the company's new A90K OLED range which features 42- and 48-inch models, the A80K in 55-,65- and 77-inch, plus there's the promise of the new X95K mini LED TV.

item.title: First look LG OLED42C2, 55-inch G2 and 77-inch OLED EVO TVs for 2022 | AVForums Podcast 24 Feb '22
item.description:
We visited LG's UK headquarters and got up close with the company's first 42-inch OLED TV. We discuss why it could be the perfect sweet spot for gamers and why it's likely to cost the same as its 48-inch C2 stable-mate. Plus we got a closer look at the new C2 and G2 OLED models which reveals some slight differences in the processing that allows a performance boost in the G2 as well as some design changes to the bezels and stands. We also compare the image of the G2 against its C2 sibling as well as last year's C1.

item.title: Dolby Vision streaming versus HDR10 disc image quality - is there a noticeable difference?
item.description:
Mark's done his homework and explains how TVs handle the colour volume and brightness data that's present on a disc or streaming movie when it exceeds the capabilities of the display itself. Then he checks out a scene in Black Widow to see if the separate HDR10 and Dolby Vision versions tell his TV to handle the image differently. His findings may surprise you.

item.title: Why are studios leaving features off their disc releases that are included on streaming?
item.description:
It seems that 4K disc collectors are being penalised by movie studios who omit features such as Dolby Vision which can be found on the film's streaming counterpart. Okay, maybe the Dolby Atmos is a touch better on the disc but there are even behind the scenes extras and IMAX Enhanced features on streaming services now. It's almost as if the studios would rather movie fans subscribe to their VOD services rather than buy their discs. Yes, Disney, we're looking at you. So what gives? And does it matter?
Email questions and feedback to podcast@avforums.com

item.title: 4K Blu ray Discs coming soon | AVForums Podcast 9 Feb '22
item.description: Among the upcoming 4K disc titles that have piqued the team's interest are The Driver, Dog Soldiers, The Usual Suspects, The Untouchables, and not one but two different Drives! There's also some discussion over the actual title of Ken Branagh's Mary Shelley's Frankenstein's Monster. The team ask whether the lo-fi Henry: Portrait of a Serial Killer will actually benefit from its 4K release and touch on a couple of new cinema releases that have unfortunately only been confirmed for 1080p Blu-ray. Plus, they discuss which Paul Thomas Anderson movie they'd each like on 4K disc and ask what the hell's happening with the Mad Max soundtrack issues.

item.title: If Filmmaker Mode looks a bit dull to your eyes initially, don't worry, there's nothing wrong!
item.description:

item.title: Philips Announce OLED807 with OLED EX Panel and more
item.description:
With the OLED807, the manufacturer is the first to reveal an OLED TV that uses the new OLED EX panel for up to 30-percent more brightness. We take a look at the other specs too, including the 6th Gen P5 AI image processing chipset and an improved Amblight system. The 8807 The One TV is a well-specified TV that includes a new 86-inch screen size, the 5th Gen P5 AI images processor, DTS Play-Fi and more... presented in a way such that the jargon and tech don't get in the way of the viewing experience.

item.title: Podcast: Is TV Calibration still relevant or does Filmmaker Mode replace it? + Movie News & Reviews
item.description:
This week we look at the latest TV news from Philips with their OLED807 TV launch, Sony has announced the A75K OLED TV for the UK and LG C2 price and availability is leaked by the John Lewis website. We also discuss the value of TV picture calibration and if it is still worthwhile doing to your new TV or does the Filmmaker Mode make it irrelevant these days? Ed also gives us a review of the Zidoo NeoS Music Streamer and his album, vinyl and playlist of the week. The movies team follow this with a review of Moonfall at the cinema as well as the latest movies release news and views, they also discuss the latest 4K Blu-ray disc announcements as well as what they have been watching on the TV. Plus, is there a big difference between Dolby Vision streaming or the HDR10 disc release of the same film?

item.title: Sony Bravia XR A80J OLED TV Review
item.description:
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/sony-a80j-xr-65a80j-4k-oled-tv-review.19352 Join the discussion - https://www.avforums.com/threads/sony-a80j-xr-65a80j-4k-oled-tv-review-comments.2395395/ While the new models for 2022 have just been announced at CES, the A80J from Sony offers superb image accuracy for movie viewing in dim surroundings with excellent sound quality thrown in for those without an external sound system. Plus, shopping around may result in a much better price than at launch as retailers move on stock for the new arrivals in the coming months. While the LG C1 is the better bet for gaming and HDMI 2.1 flexibility, the Sony A80J offers highly detailed image quality with superb video processing and motion. Added to this is incredible image quality for critical movie viewing with stunning colour accuracy and superb tone mapping, bringing movies to life with excellent cinematic flair. Today’s OLED market is tough with many great TVs offering their own pros and cons, but for movie fans, the Sony really does offer great calibrated image quality and features and comes highly recommended for that use.

item.title: Samsung QN95A Neo QLED Mini LED TV Review
item.description:
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/samsung-qn95a-qe65qn95a-neo-qled-mini-led-tv-review.19416 Join the discussion - https://www.avforums.com/threads/samsung-qn95a-qe65qn95a-neo-qled-mini-led-tv-review-comments.2393759/ The Samsung QN95A is the flagship 4K LED LCD NEO QLED TV for 2021 and offers very good performance across the board for those looking for an all-round TV for bright and darkroom viewing. It offers a peak brightness of 1588 nits in the most accurate HDR Filmmaker Mode with a full-screen brightness of 675 nits, providing an excellent dynamic range for HDR10 content. Black levels are also, for the majority, solid and detailed with good shadow retrieval and decent local dimming thanks to those thousands of Mini LEDs in the backlight. There are still some issues with the Local Dimming affecting peak highlights in some mixed scenes by dimming down the brightness on offer, as well as some dirty screen effect and black crush, but this is much improved over previous years' models thanks to those Mini LEDs and better local dimming algorithms. Overall, with HDMI 2.1 gaming features, excellent smart TV and strong HDR brightness with superb calibrated colour and greyscale, the QN95A does live up to its flagship status and comes recommended for those looking for a good quality all-round living room TV.
We use (www.portrait.com) Portrait Displays' Calman color calibration software, a Murideo Seven Generator and Klein K-10A meter for measurement and calibration.

item.title: Samsung AU9000 4K LED LCD TV Review
item.description:
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/samsung-au9000-ue50au9000-led-lcd-tv-review.19322 The Samsung AU9000 is not an enthusiast’s TV for critical movie viewing in a dark room, and it never pretends to be. It is a good quality everyday living room workhorse with a decent image for bright room viewing that gets fairly accurate out of the box. It has an excellent smart TV system and gaming features such as ALLM, VRR and a low input lag of 10.9ms to keep the most competitive gamer happy. It does struggle with HDR image brightness and there is no Dolby Vision on board, but it also comes in at a very competitive price point, where it offers decent value for money and gets a recommendation if you are looking for such a screen.
We use (www.portrait.com) Portrait Displays' Calman color calibration software, a Murideo Seven Generator and Klein K-10A meter for measurement and calibration.

item.title: Philips OLED+936 4K OLED TV Review
item.description:
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/philips-936-65oled-936-oled-tv-review.19274 The OLED+936 is positioned as a luxury high-end OLED TV with the added sound quality of a Bowers & Wilkins speaker bar and a design that includes decent materials and excellent build quality. It offers picture quality to rival the big names on the market and marries this with a functional OS and Smart TV system and the major USP of Ambilight. It has the new Emission Layer panel boasting a 20% brightness increase, all the major HDR formats and support for both DTS and Dolby Atmos audio via the 3.1.2 Bowers & Wilkins speaker bar. Plus, it offers calibrated image quality that matches the competition and adds in HDMI 2.1 with VRR, AMD FreeSync Premium and ALLM for gaming. Overall, it comes highly recommended and should be on your demo lists.
We use (www.portrait.com) Portrait Displays' Calman color calibration software, a Murideo Seven Generator and Klein K-10A meter for measurement and calibration.

item.title: Panasonic JZ2000 4K OLED TV Review
item.description:
The Panasonic TX-55JZ2000B offers some of the best SDR and HDR images we have seen so far this year. Head to AVForums to read the full in-depth review.
Where the JZ1500 is the choice for those who don’t need the Dolby Atmos sound system and just want the Custom Professional Panel, the Panasonic JZ2000 remains the flagship model offering all the options. There are a few niggles with a performance that is a very slight step back compared to the HZ2000 from last year, and if you don’t need HDMI 2.1 you could seek one out, but the overall performance and new gaming features, still make the JZ2000 a compelling purchase. If you want the best SDR and HDR cinematic images available on a 2021 OLED TV, along with strong gaming features and the soundbar and up-firing speakers, the JZ2000 comes highly recommended.

item.title: Philips 48 inch OLED806 Review
item.description:
Philips adds a 48-inch screen size to its OLED range with the 48OLED806 which includes all the current HDR formats including both HDR10+ and Dolby Vision, plus two new HDMI 2.1 full bandwidth inputs and gaming features such as VRR, AMD FreeSync Premium and ALLM, a first for the brand.
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/philips-48-inch-806-48oled806-oled-tv-review.19272
Added to the feature list is the Philips TV USP of Ambilight, a full-on, four-sided bias lighting system that can be used to combat eye fatigue when viewing in a dark room, or for adding lighting effects that follow the action on screen for complete immersion. It’s a fantastic feature only available on Philips TVs.
And overall, the OLED806 directly competes with the LG 48C1 and does so with some strong image quality, excellent motion and video processing, along with accurate calibrated images and very good sound quality. There is more competition than ever at the 48-inch screen size and the Philips puts together a very strong proposition that comes highly recommended.
We use (www.portrait.com) Portrait Displays' Calman color calibration software, a Murideo Seven Generator and Klein K-10A meter for measurement and calibration.

item.title: Hisense A7G QLED TV Review
item.description:
We take a look at the Hisense A7G, an entry-level QLED model with HDR10, HDR10+, HLG and Dolby Vision compatibility as well as HDMI 2.1 eARC, ALLM and VRR features for gaming and Dolby Atmos sound decoding.
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/hisense-a7g-50a7gq-qled-tv-review.18808
The A7G is also a QLED TV with Quantum Dot technology built into the panel to give purer looking colours, although it doesn’t quite reach the full width of the DCI-P3 colour gamut for HDR, instead Hisense states 90% coverage. Other features include an AI picture processor for upscaling, and Dolby Atmos support for immersive audio is also built-in though the TV obviously only has two speakers.
The A7GQ also features Hisense’s propriety smart TV system, VIDAA U5.0, as well as Freeview Play with all the UK terrestrial catch-up apps and services. The VIDAA system is intuitive to use and runs at a decent speed from button press to app opening and playing, plus there is Netflix, Prime Video and YouTube in 4K HDR. There is a content discovery feature along with direct one-press buttons on the remote and there is also compatibility with Alexa for voice commands.
The A7G is a TV that has been built to a price point and market segment, offering some decent features within the overall package, so is it worth considering as the main living room TV or is it more suited as a bedroom or second room unit? Let’s find out…
We use (www.portrait.com) Portrait Displays' Calman color calibration software, a Murideo Seven Generator and Klein K-10A meter for measurement and calibration.

media:group.media:title: Hisense A7G QLED TV Review
media:group.media:description:
We take a look at the Hisense A7G, an entry-level QLED model with HDR10, HDR10+, HLG and Dolby Vision compatibility as well as HDMI 2.1 eARC, ALLM and VRR features for gaming and Dolby Atmos sound decoding.
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/hisense-a7g-50a7gq-qled-tv-review.18808
The A7G is also a QLED TV with Quantum Dot technology built into the panel to give purer looking colours, although it doesn’t quite reach the full width of the DCI-P3 colour gamut for HDR, instead Hisense states 90% coverage. Other features include an AI picture processor for upscaling, and Dolby Atmos support for immersive audio is also built-in though the TV obviously only has two speakers.
The A7GQ also features Hisense’s propriety smart TV system, VIDAA U5.0, as well as Freeview Play with all the UK terrestrial catch-up apps and services. The VIDAA system is intuitive to use and runs at a decent speed from button press to app opening and playing, plus there is Netflix, Prime Video and YouTube in 4K HDR. There is a content discovery feature along with direct one-press buttons on the remote and there is also compatibility with Alexa for voice commands.
The A7G is a TV that has been built to a price point and market segment, offering some decent features within the overall package, so is it worth considering as the main living room TV or is it more suited as a bedroom or second room unit? Let’s find out…
We use (www.portrait.com) Portrait Displays' Calman color calibration software, a Murideo Seven Generator and Klein K-10A meter for measurement and calibration.

item.title: Panasonic JZ1500 OLED TV Review: Is this the Home Cinema Screen of the Year?
item.description:
The Panasonic TX-65JZ1500B offers some of the best SDR and HDR images we have seen so far this year in a package that AVForums readers have been demanding for some time. Gone are the soundbar and up-firing speakers but the panel is now the top of the range Custom Professional Panel with the heat sink and increased brightness, giving enthusiasts a monitor-like package for use with their existing sound systems. Added to this is the usual accuracy out of the box for TV and film content added to new gaming features and most catch up apps and you almost have a full-on package for the film fan. There are a few niggles that stop it from attaining a Best in Class rating, but it does come highly recommended!

item.title: Sony BRAVIA XR A90J OLED TV Review: Plus comparisons with Panasonic JZ1500, LG G1 & C1 OLED TVs
item.description:
The Sony A90J is one of the best SDR and HDR performers for 2021 with accurate image quality following calibration and some of the most impactful HDR thanks to the new XR OLED Contrast Pro technology. Added to this is the Acoustic Surface Audio+ technology that turns the screen into the speaker as well as Google TV replacing Android as the OS and smart TV system. It is lacking terrestrial apps such as iPlayer at the time of the review, but Sony insists this will be rectified in the near future with a firmware update. If you’re a movie fan looking for some of the best SDR and HDR OLED image quality, you really should demo the Sony BRAVIA XR A90J, which comes highly recommended!
We use (www.portrait.com) Portrait Displays' Calman color calibration software, a Murideo Seven Generator and Klein K-10A meter for measurement and calibration.

item.title: Samsung QN900A 8K Neo QLED Mini LED TV Review
item.description:
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/samsung-qn900-qe75qn900a-neo-qled-8k-tv-review.18744
The Samsung QN900A is the company's flagship Neo QLED TV for 2021, which means it includes every design feature and technology the Korean giant has to offer. The QN900 uses an 8K panel with a newly developed Quantum Mini-LED backlight for a slimmer design and more dimmable zones. It also uses quantum dot filters for an increased colour volume, the latest AI-enhanced Neo Quantum Processor, and supports high dynamic range, including HDR10+ Adaptive.
The ultra-slim design uses a bezel-less screen with a filter to reject ambient light and widen the viewing angles. There's a newly slimmed-down One Connect box that can now be attached to the back of the stand if you prefer, four HDMI 2.1 ports, and a solar-powered remote control. There's OTS Pro sound with a total of ten speakers cleverly hidden in the edge and rear of the panel, along with a comprehensive smart platform and all the latest gaming features.
Unsurprisingly there's no support for Dolby Vision, nor is there onboard Dolby Atmos decoding, although the QN900A can send Atmos back from its internal apps via ARC. These two things aside, it includes every feature you would expect from a modern high-end TV. Unfortunately, it also comes with an equally high-end price, and the 75-inch model being reviewed here will set you back an eye-watering £7,499. Can the Samsung QE75QN900A possibly justify this premium? Let's find out...

item.title: LG C1 OLED TV Review: Is this the best all-round OLED TV of 2021?
item.description:
The LG C1, like previous C models, is the sweet spot in the 2021 OLED TV range from LG and offers a few small upgrades over last year’s CX.
Read the full in-depth review - https://www.avforums.com/reviews/lg-c1-oled65c1-4k-oled-tv-review.18726
The design of the C1 hasn’t changed much at all from previous generations and has the same stand designs and chassis layout, but this year there are slight colour changes. The stand on our review model was a silver finish with a white rear to the panel that LG calls Vanilla. If you want a dark coloured rear then it is called Meteor Titan. A new remote control was also introduced this year along with new menu designs and a new look WebOS 6.0 smart system which you will either love or hate, more on that later.
The C1 supports most of the HDR formats including HDR10, HLG (Hybrid Log-Gamma), Dolby Vision and Dolby Vision IQ and the excellent Filmmaker Mode that matches industry standards for content mastering. There is no HDR10+ support, but we don’t see an issue with that, given the small amount of content that uses the format.
LG has partnered with NVIDIA and AMD to make LG OLED TVs the only G-SYNC and AMD FreeSync™ Premium certified TVs available to date. There is also a new Game Optimiser set up menu and there are four HDMI 2.1 (40 Gbps) inputs with support for 4K/120, HFR (High Frame Rate), VRR (Variable Refresh Rate), ALLM (Auto Low Latency Mode) and eARC. We also have HGiG (HDR Gaming Interest Group) settings available for HDR gaming.
So is the C1 a major upgrade to the CX? Or even competition to the G1? Let’s find out.

item.title: Podcast: LG C1 Review, Apple Lossless & Dolby Atmos @ no cost, Sennheiser IE900 review + more
item.description:
This week we round off the C1 OLED TV review and also cover the answers to our questions regarding the EVO panel and processing in the C1 and G1 from LG. Ed reviews the Sennheiser IE 900 earphones and we discuss the recent news that Apple will offer lossless music and Dolby Atmos for no additional costs on their Apple Music service, while Amazon drops the subscription costs of its Lossless music service. Plus, Tom is here to cover the latest movie and TV Show news and reviews.
Presented by Phil Hinton with Ed Selley and Tom Davies
Email questions and feedback to podcast@avforums.com

item.description:
This week Steve looks at the REL T/9x subwoofer and Ed is reviewing the Bowers & Wilkins PI7 in-ear headphones, while Greg is meshing his Wi-Fi with the Netgear RBK853 Tri-band Mesh WiFi 6 System.
